headline: Punjab AAP delays ministers’ list, new probables emerge
content: The delay by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in announcing its ministers as candidates from their respective constituencies has started becoming a headache for them, with fresh aspirants emerging within the party.Their rivals, not just in Opposition parties but also within the AAP, have started taking potshots at them, even questioning their winnability. In Jalandhar, the party has announced candidates for eight of the nine Assembly seats.The only ticket yet to be announced is that of Cabinet Minister Mohinder Bhagat from Jalandhar West (reserved). Bhagat holds the portfolios of Defence Services Welfare, Freedom Fighters and Horticulture.Amid the delay, several ticket aspirants within the party have started staking their claim to the seat. Among the prominent contenders are Amritpal Singh, Chairman of the District Planning Committee, Jalandhar, and youth leader Robin Sampla.Sampla met AAP Punjab in-charge Manish Sisodia a few days ago to stake his claim. His social media teams have also been actively projecting him as the most deserving candidate.In a bid to counter the claims of other aspirants and pre-empt any possible dissent, Bhagat opened a new office at Babrik Chowk on Sunday and also organised a havan.Son of former BJP minister Bhagat Chunni Lal, Mohinder Bhagat had contested the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections from the seat as a BJP candidate but lost on both occasions.In March 2024, Sheetal Angural, who had won the seat as an AAP candidate, quit the party. A bypoll was held in June 2024, during which both Angural and Bhagat switched parties. Angural contested as the BJP candidate, while Bhagat joined the AAP and won by 37,000 votes.On the delay in the announcement of his candidature, Bhagat said, “It is part of the party’s strategy to announce the tickets of MLAs first and then those of halqa in-charges, whose candidature could be doubtful. They are the ones who need to be assured so that they can prepare better. The names of ministers will come in the third or fourth list.”On new claimants emerging from within the party, Bhagat said, “That is the beauty of democracy. Everyone has the right to stake a claim.”Explaining the need for a new office, he said, “I already have a permanent office in Basti Nau, but it is located in an internal lane and visitors face parking issues. The new location at Babrik Chowk will make me more accessible to the public while also taking care of parking issues.”

headline: Calcutta High Court extends interim protection to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee till February 26 in six criminal cases
content: Kolkata The Calcutta High Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) extended interim protection from coercive action to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee in six criminal cases lodged against him at various police stations in West Bengal. https://www.thehindu.com/elections/candidates/LokSabha2024/abhishek-banerjee-9008/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/ Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya extended the protection in two separate petitions filed by Mr. Banerjee in connection with the six cases registered against him since May this year. Comments by Abhishek Banerjee painful but not contemptuous: Calcutta High Court Comments by Abhishek Banerjee painful but not contemptuous: Calcutta High Court The development comes days after Justice Krishna Rao of the Calcutta High Court on November 17 issued criminal contempt proceedings against Abhishek Banerjee for remarks made on November 7 Comments by Abhishek Banerjee painful but not contemptuous: Calcutta High Court storyline 1 The interim protection granted to the Diamond Harbour MP will remain in force till February 26, 2027, or until further orders, whichever is earlier. Hearing a petition seeking extension of the protection granted to him on August 25 in three of the cases, Justice Bhattacharyya noted that the investigations were yet to be completed and there had been no change in circumstances warranting denial of the extension sought by Mr. Banerjee. Calcutta High Court grants protection to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee from arrest in three cases storyline 1 Additional Advocate General Billwadal Bhattacharya, appearing for the state in connection with the three cases, submitted that a special leave petition (SLP) had been filed before the Supreme Court challenging the high court’s August 25 order and that it was pending consideration. Seeking an extension of the interim protection, Mr. Banerjee’s counsel Gopal Sankaranarayan told the court that the SLP pending before the Supreme Court was a defective appeal. The State had opposed Banerjee’s plea for extension of the interim protection granted by the High Court on August 25. Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek The supporters of Trinamool had gathered outside the police station in support of Abhishek Banerjee Trinamool supporters attacked outside the police station as police questioned Abhishek storyline 1 The protection from coercive action by police in these three cases relates to FIRs registered at Bhowanipore, Bishnupur and Kalitala police stations. In connection with three other cases registered at Rabindranagar and Bishnupur police stations in South 24 Parganas district, the state submitted communications detailing the progress of investigations in two of them. Mr. Sankaranarayan sought an extension of the interim protection granted to Banerjee on September 7 in connection with these three cases. Additional Advocate General Rajdeep Majumdar, appearing for the state, opposed the plea. Noting that investigations in the three cases were continuing, Justice Bhattacharyya extended the interim protection from coercive action till February 26, 2027, or until further orders, whichever is earlier.

headline: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
content:
Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal PM Balen Shah | Photo Credit: AP

The Prime Minister of Nepal, Balendra Shah, arrived in New Delhi on Sunday (November 22, 2026) afternoon for his first official visit to India. The Prime Ministers of both the countries inaugurated the Saryu-Kamala rail service from Ayodhya to Janakpur, Nepal and Dharchula road bridge between Uttarakhand and Nepal, through video conferencing.

According to sources, Monday’s (November 23, 2026) discussion between the two Prime Ministers will give “political direction” to bilateral relations for the coming years.

Mr. Shah is leading a 34-member delegation that includes his Chief Advisor Kumar Byanjankar, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Minister for Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal. A separate business delegation is also visiting India along with the Prime Minister’s delegation.

“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.

PM Modi announced that India will establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Nepal, alongside a startup incubator and an innovation hub, as part of a broader push to empower Nepali youth and deepen bilateral educational and technological cooperation.

headline: India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari
content: Kolkata India is facing challenges on several fronts which includes a gradual movement towards an authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Hamid Ansari said. Mr. Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan, highlighted three point challenges faced by the country, which includes the pursuit of neoliberal policies, sharpening of communal polarisation and the movement towards authoritarian rule. “This threefold attack includes the aggressive pursuit of neoliberal policies of economic reforms. Secondly, the relentless onslaught on the secular democratic foundations of the Indian republic by sharpening of communal polarisation, and thirdly, the movement towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions and methods of which are considered sacrosanct in a democracy,” the former Vice-President said. From Sept 2026: Former V-P Hamid Ansari’s remarks exposed ‘Muslim League-Maoist character’ of Congress, says BJP https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/former-v-p-hamid-ansaris-remarks-exposed-muslim-league-maoist-character-of-congress-says-bjp/article71491220.ece Recalling the contribution of the late Sitaram Yechury. Mr Ansari said that the CPI(M) spoke against the certain ideological position in which nationalism has only been equated with Hindu nationalism. “Bharat Mata has no Hinduism in naturalism. This is not a Bharat Mata that has given birth to Muslims, Christians, Tarsus, Buddhists, Jains, and atheists,” Mr. Ansari quoted Mr. Yechury from one of his speeches in 2017. The former Vice-President also said Mr. Yechury opined that the struggle against imperialist aggression, the imposition of neoliberal order, and fundamentalism should be welded together to form a powerful anti-imperialist movement. He emphasised the need to maintain multilateralism in external affairs so as not to compromise on foreign policy positions, Mr. Ansari recalled that Mr. Yechury, despite some frictions within the CPI(M) and with the Congress, formed a strong relationship with the Congress leadership, particularly with Sonia Gandhi and the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi. He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government. He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. This is usually strange. The Congress accepted many of the suggestions to ensure a working majority,” he added. Meanwhile, general secretary of CPI(M) M.A. Baby, Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera, renowned economist Prabhat Patnaik, historian Mukul Kesavan, and distinguished scholar Malini Bhattacharya were also present in the seminar in Kolkata on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Addressing the seminar, Mr. Baby said that imperialism has reached a diabolical and barbaric stage across the world today. “Before Israel was to launch an attack on Iran without any rhyme or reason, the Prime Minister of India goes to Israel and addresses the Israeli Parliament two days ahead oftime. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism. In his lecture, Mr. Patnaik discussed the current problems of capitalism, and called capitalism the basis of imperialism. He said that imperialism now looks so desperate and is causing an international crisis for which we still don’t have a clear answer. But he viewed the problems of capitalism are reasons behind such desperation. “The U.S. is trying to capture and acquire control over the entire world’s oil resources. In order to buy oil futures, they have to pay dollars. So, the demand for dollars cannot drop much “ He argued to show the USA’s desperation to capture the world’s precious resources through a recolonisation process. The Cuban Ambassador recalled Mr. Yechury’s contribution to strengthening India’s ties to Cuba. “He publicly reaffirmed his support to the Cuban people, recalling the difficult circumstances Cuba faced during the special period after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the resilience of the Cuban people and the role of the Communist Party of Cuba in building the unity that has ensured popular support to the revolution,” he said.

headline: CPI(M) hails Kerala High Court relief to protesting Sanskrit University students as a slap in the face to the VC and UDF government
content: Thiruvananthapuram The Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the Kerala High Court’s order quashing the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in Kalady was a “resounding slap in the face” to Higher Education Minister Roji M. John and the varsity vice-chancellor (Dr. Ciza John). https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/ CPI(M) State Secretary M.V. Govindan told reporters that Mr. John had actively aided the vice-chancellor, whom he portrayed as a Sangh Parivar enabler, to suspend the students, all Student Federation of India (SFI) activists, and deny them their right to appear for examinations. “Mr. John had revealed his true political colours. He demanded the students apologise to the vice-chancellor or forfeit their future”, he said. Relief for suspended Sanskrit varsity students, Kerala High Court quashes suspension, guilty report Relief for suspended Sanskrit varsity students, Kerala High Court quashes suspension, guilty report The University was also instructed to hold a separate examination for the suspended students, as undertaken before the Supreme Court, within six weeks Relief for suspended Sanskrit varsity students, Kerala High Court quashes suspension, guilty report storyline 1 Mr. Govindan said Mr. John’s demand that the students apologise had jarred Keralam’s civil society. “His demand was a hark back to the tradition of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leaders to apologise to colonial rulers and to become their eager acolytes to sabotage India’s storied Independence Struggle. The students spurned Mr. John’s demand and shrugged off the vice-chancellor’s threats and fought for their political cause”, he said. Mr. Govindan said the CPI(M) was loath to borrow the humiliating word, “apologise”, from Mr. John’s and the Sangh Parivar’s “shared lexicon”. “Instead, the CPI(M) is daring Mr. John to show the moral courage to admit he and his government had erred in playing second fiddle to the RSS-appointed vice-chancellor”, he said. High Court relief sparks celebrations as 16 suspended SSUS students return to Kalady University campus in victory march High Court relief sparks celebrations as 16 suspended SSUS students return to Kalady University campus in victory march The suspended students were then taken to the SSUS campus in a triumphant march carrying a banner that read, “The people united will never be defeated” High Court relief sparks celebrations as 16 suspended SSUS students return to Kalady University campus in victory march storyline 1 Mr. Govindan said the High Court directive to conduct special examinations for the striking students, all hailing from working-class families, was a moral win for students’ rights and democracy. “To Mr. John’s and the vice-chancellor’s chagrin, the High Court had also insulated the students from their joint and strident demand for an apology for a foisted offence”, he said. He said Mr. John and the vice-chancellor had punished the students for demanding basic campus infrastructure, including the lack of lecturers and delay in awarding fellowships. “However, the High Court came to the students’ rescue”, he added.

headline: CPI(M) accuses Keralam CM V.D. Satheesan of turning political pay back into policy
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] on Monday (November 23, 2026) accused Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of turning political pay back into policy. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/communist-party-of-india-marxist/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/ V.D. Satheesan | The ‘Nehruvian’ revivalist storyline 1 CPI(M) State secretary M.V. Govindan told reporters that Mr. Satheesan had violated his oath of office by publicly announcing that his government would go hard on political opponents using instruments of executive power, including law enforcement. UDF govt. smacks of corruption and nepotism: Keralam BJP general secretary UDF govt. smacks of corruption and nepotism: Keralam BJP general secretary The UDF government has amply demonstrated that it lacked collective responsibility and coordination in the honeymoon period itself, he says UDF govt. smacks of corruption and nepotism: Keralam BJP general secretary storyline 1 Mr. Satheesan’s controversial speech at a Youth Congress “Generation India Campaign” rally in Kannur on November 20 had prompted the CPI(M) reaction. Mr. Satheesan said his government was born of the blood and tears of party workers, who bore the brunt of the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government’s warlike stance against opposition activists. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/left-democratic-front/ “We will seek revenge. It’s not like old times, when the political norm was to forget and forgive opponents upon assuming power. That old convention is passe. We saw a lot of bloodshed and violence against our student and youth organisation activists. We can’t stop thinking about the suffering of our brethren, which laid the groundwork for the Congress’s comeback to power. We have tried to forget and failed. We will serve our tormentors retribution. We don’t want the glamour of being forgiving. The recent investigations and constitution of SIT’s are a demonstration of our will to bring the violators to book. Those who are responsible for the transgressions will go to jail. We will fight till the last breath to ensure their incarceration”, Mr. Satheesan had said. Also Read : UDF convenor dares V.D. Satheesan reveal name of ‘anonymous benefactor’ who sponsored his chartered flight https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/kerala/udf-convenor-dares-vd-satheesan-reveal-name-of-anonymous-benefactor-who-sponsored-his-chartered-flight/article71602592.ece Mr. Govindan said that there seemed to be no limit to Mr. Satheesan’s vindictiveness. “The Chief Minister’s open threat to dish out revenge to those whom he perceives as enemies and weaponise law enforcement to target political opponents amounts to criminal intimidation and a brazen and public violation of his oath of office. The CPI(M) will seek legal and political recourse to bring Mr. Satheesan to account and prevent him from setting new and dangerous precedents for democracy”. The UDF government had, from the outset, demonstrated its political resolve to go after those responsible for the “attacks and false cases” against Kerala Students Union (KSU) and Youth Congress during the previous LDF dispensation. Pinarayi Vijayan hails Kalady students’ victory after court relief Pinarayi Vijayan hails Kalady students’ victory after court relief This struggle, waged with the firm conviction that they would not apologise for something they had not done, serves as a source of motivation for every student seeking to defend democratic rights on campuses, Mr. Vijayan said Pinarayi Vijayan hails Kalady students’ victory after court relief storyline 1 Notably, the UDF’s first Cabinet meeting after assuming power in May formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the police action against KSU workers who staged a roadside black flag protest against the LDF’s Nava Kerala Sadas programme in Alappuzha in 2023. Former Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) M.R. Ajith Kumar and former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan’s personal security detail were under the ambit of the SIT probe.

headline: India announces development package over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal’s development
content: New Delhi Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday (November 23, 2026) announced a development package of ₹15,000 (24,000 crore Nepalese rupees) for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/Narendra_Modi/ Balendra Shah | Enigmatic mayor storyline 1 The two leaders virtually laid the foundation of several India-assisted projects in Nepal and flagged off a cross-border passenger rail link between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Also Read: Nepal PM India visit updates on November 23, 2026 https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/nepal-pm-india-visit-balen-shah-begins-bilateral-trip-energy-connectivity-on-agenda-live-updates-november-23-2026/article71733252.ece Nepal’s PM Shah landed in New Delhi on a two-day visit on Sunday (November 22), intending to inject new momentum into the bilateral ties that came under some strain in May following PM Shah's remarks seeking involvement of China and the United Kingdom to address the long-standing border dispute between India and Nepal. http://thehindu.com/news/national/no-role-for-any-third-parties-in-resolution-of-india-nepal-border-issue-mea/article71052660.ece "The relations between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as the oceans," the Nepalese leader said in his media statement. PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, on a two-day State visit, laid a wreath at Raj Ghat and received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan before the talks at Hyderabad House PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda storyline 1 "As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal," he said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations. In his remarks, PM Modi also highlighted the strength of India-Nepal ties and how New Delhi is committed to extend all possible support for development and prosperity of the neighbouring nation. Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter The approval is valid from November 17, 2026, to July 31, 2027, and is expected to help Nepal manage the seasonal gap between electricity demand and domestic generation Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter storyline 1 "The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely that of neighbours, but it is about kinship and unbreakable trust. We share our joys and challenges," he said. "We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in difficult times," he said. The Prime Minister expressed India's deep condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. "And today, to give renewed strength to Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development, we announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees," he said. PM Modi also made a mention of India's assistance to Nepal in the energy sector. "India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential goods to Nepal for many years. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First policy, despite serious challenges related to oil supply this year, we have maintained the supply of fuel, fertilisers and other essential goods to Nepal," he said. Nepal’s plea at climate summit reveals limits of loss and damage finance Nepal’s plea at climate summit reveals limits of loss and damage finance Four years after governments promised help for countries battered by climate disasters, Nepal’s appeal in Türkiye exposes how little money is available Nepal’s plea at climate summit reveals limits of loss and damage finance storyline 1 The two sides inked several agreements to expand cooperation in specific sectors, including health and education. In his comments, Nepal’s PM Shah said his talks with Prime Minister Modi were aimed at further strengthening and modernising the centuries-old Nepal-India relationship. "The need of the hour is to stand on the sturdy foundation of this enduring bond of friendship and build strong pillars of cooperation for the future," the Nepalese leader said. "I am confident that the outcomes we reached today will elevate Nepal-India ties to new heights," he said.

headline: West Bengal to be renamed as Paschim Banga
content: Kolkata A proposal to rename West Bengal as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be tabled in the State Assembly on December 9, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday (November 23, 2026). The announcement was made after a Cabinet meeting at the State Secretariat. “West Bengal will be known as ‘Paschim Banga’ in English as well. The name must be written exactly as ‘Paschim Banga’. We will introduce a resolution in the Assembly on the 9th. After its passage, it will be sent to the Government of India for the necessary parliamentary and legal procedures,” Mr. Adhikari said. The State is referred to as ‘Paschim Banga’ in Bengali language and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government wants the same name to be used in English. “The formation of West Bengal has a history dating back to June 20, 1947, and that history must be recognised. Instead of ‘West Bengal’, the name will be ‘Paschim Banga’,” the Chief Minister said. The BJP leadership in West Bengal has often emphasised that the word Paschim Banga is part of the history of the creation of the State, which bears the brunt of partition and one part of the State became East Bengal [Purba Bangla] which is now Bangladesh. By using the name Paschim Banga, the BJP wants to highlight how Syama Prasad Mookerjee and others sought the State as a homeland for “ Bengali Hindus” during partition of the country. The Bharatiya Janata Party government, had earlier this year, observed June 20 as Paschimbanga Divas, marking the date in 1947, when Jana Sangha founder Syama Prasad Mookerjee moved a proposal in the Bengal Legislative Assembly to partition Bengal. The Trinamool Congress government had passed a resolution to name West Bengal as Bangla in July 2018, but the Union government did not consider Mamata Banerjee’ government’s repeated requests to change the State’s official name to ‘Bangla’. EOM

headline: Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from Kallakurichi Collector over TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told
content: CHENNAI State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arun Vignesh of misbehaving with her, as widely reported in the media over the past few days. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026). HC judge’s reference to ‘harassment’ of Kallakurichi Collector triggers call for action against TVK MLA HC judge’s reference to ‘harassment’ of Kallakurichi Collector triggers call for action against TVK MLA At a Gender Sensitisation Committee and Internal Complaints Committee (GSICC) - II meeting in Madurai on Saturday, Justice L. Victoria Gowri of the Madras High Court, said “When high ranking officers themselves were insecure, one can imagine the plight of ordinary persons.” HC judge’s reference to ‘harassment’ of Kallakurichi Collector triggers call for action against TVK MLA storyline 1 The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer. When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case. National Commission for Women calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi MLA-Collector issue National Commission for Women calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi MLA-Collector issue Chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has written to the Tamil Nadu DGP seeking a fair enquiry into the allegations that Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh sent obscene WhatsApp messages to J.E. Padmaja, the District Collector. National Commission for Women calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi MLA-Collector issue storyline 1 “Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?” The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.” Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims Ms. Padmaja is an honest officer “who acted strictly in accordance with the law, without yielding to either the ruling party or the opposition,” said the Minister from VCK, an ally in the TVK-led coalition government. Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims storyline 1 On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.” ‘Won’t interfere if there’s no plaint’ Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.” DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector The MLA had denied sending any such message to the collector; DMK chief Stalin said CM Vijay should take ‘real action’ against erring MLAs instead of delivering ‘punch dialogues’ DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector storyline 1 After taking note of the SPP’s submission that the State was willing to file an affidavit before the court making it clear that neither the police nor the Chief Secretary had received any complaint from the woman IAS officer, the judge asked Mr. Sathyan to get in touch with the woman IAS officer, too, and obtain instructions by Tuesday (November 24, 2026) as to whether she had lodged any complaint.

headline: Supreme Court bars Tamil Nadu government from coercive action against SASTRA University over land dispute
content: New Delhi The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) admitted an appeal filed by Shanmugha Arts Science Technology and Research Academy (SASTRA), a deemed university based in Thanjavur, against a Madras High Court direction to the Tamil Nadu government to evict it from 31.37 acres of public land in its occupation for nearly 40 years. The Court had already stayed the eviction of the university in an order passed on January 15, 2026, and had allowed the institution to carry out its activities without any hindrance. Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu government to consider alternative site rather than evicting SASTRA varsity Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu government to consider alternative site rather than evicting SASTRA varsity If someone was running a resort or a commercial complex or having a shopping mall there or having immoral or illegal activity there, we would have thrown them out, said the CJI Supreme Court asks Tamil Nadu government to consider alternative site rather than evicting SASTRA varsity storyline 1 At that hearing, the Court asked the State government to consider three options of alternative lands offered by the university, instead of the land occupied and already utilised by it, represented by senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi. A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had found the three options “just and fair”, and asked the State to consider the offer “sympathetically and take an appropriate decision by ensuring that no loss is caused to the public exchequer”. It also suggested that a high-powered committee of three senior officers of the State government accord a personal hearing to the university to “explain all the attending circumstances and also to persuade the authorities to accept one of the three options”. Evict SASTRA University from 31.37 acres of government land, says Madras High Court Evict SASTRA University from 31.37 acres of government land, says Madras High Court The Third Division Bench of Justices S.M. Subramaniam and C. Kumarappan says that the Thanjavur Collector can seek the assitance of the police, if required, for the eviction within four weeks Evict SASTRA University from 31.37 acres of government land, says Madras High Court storyline 1 On August 10, 2026, the Court gave the State, represented by senior advocate Jaideep Gupta and Tamil Nadu Additional Advocate General Haripriya Padmanabhan, a “free hand in determining the actual market value of land” under dispute, with the university obligated to pay. The August order also recorded the university’s offer to pay the sale price of any land the State required for a public purpose, in this case the establishment of a prison, for which it wanted the disputed 31.37-acre property. The Court asked the State to take a “reasonably fair decision and apprise this court”. However, at the next hearing on September 21, 2026, the State sought more time to “consider the different options”. At the September 21 hearing, the Court noted that the land in dispute was used by an educational institution serving a public purpose, and asked why the State was so “obstinate” on eviction and demolition of the institution. The State government had contended that the alternate parcels were inferior to the disputed land in terms of value, accessibility and contiguity, and that settling for alternative land could amount to putting a premium on encroachment. But the Chief Justice pointed out that the dispute concerned an educational institution. “If someone was running a resort there, or running a commercial complex, or having a shopping mall there, or having immoral or illegal activity there, we would have thrown them out,” he had said. On Monday (November 23, 2026), the State leaned against settling for alternative sites. Granting leave to SASTRA’s appeal, the Court issued a rule nisi, which means the State would have to show cause why it wants to contest the appeal rather than settle for any of the three alternative options. The State said it would file a response.

headline: PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda
content: New Delhi Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah arrived at Hyderabad House on Monday (November 23, 2026) to hold bilateral talks, to review India-Nepal relations and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation across key sectors. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/Narendra_Modi/ Balendra Shah | Enigmatic mayor storyline 1 story Celebrating 100 years: The tale of Delhi's iconic Hyderabad House A worker carrying the tricolour along a corridor of the Hyderabad House in New Delhi ahead of a high-profile event. The building, designed by Edwin Lutyens for the last Nizam of Hyderabad, is now used by the Central government to host diplomatic events and meetings. The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. Also read: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: Balen Shah begins bilateral visit; energy, connectivity on agenda https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/nepal-pm-india-visit-balen-shah-begins-bilateral-trip-energy-connectivity-on-agenda-live-updates-november-23-2026/article71733252.ece Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development. Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit. The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation. headline: Congress MLA Gokul Setia writes letter in blood to Haryana CM, claims briefly detained by police
content: Sirsa Congress Sirsa MLA Gokul Setia on Sunday (November 22, 2026) claimed he was briefly detained by police as he wanted to give Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini a letter written in blood to highlight multiple civic issues in his constituency. Mr. Saini, however, denied the MLA's claim. Mr. Saini was in Sirsa to flag off the Kalanwali Youth Marathon, aimed at spreading awareness against drug abuse and encouraging youngsters to take up sports and adopt a healthy lifestyle, and to chair a meeting of the District Grievance Redressal Committee. Mr. Setia had earlier said that he would sit at Shaheed Bhagat Singh Chowk on Sunday (November 22) morning and write a letter using his blood to draw the government's attention to the issues in his constituency. Congress-SP seat-sharing talks likely on November 23 Congress-SP seat-sharing talks likely on November 23 Congress is hopeful of forging an alliance with the Samajwadi Party (SP) for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election but wants a “respectable” seat-sharing arrangement, says All India Congress Committee in-charge for the State Rajendra Pal Gautam Congress-SP seat-sharing talks likely on November 23 storyline 1 "When people of Sirsa are shedding tears of blood, is it not my duty to stand in their support? Don't we say that we will give our blood and sweat for our people," the MLA told the media on Sunday (November 22). "I was not raising any party slogan, I only wanted to hand over the letter to the chief minister. But I was detained by such heavy police force which they had deployed to stop me," he said. He asked why the government was so scared that heavy police deployment was made to stop him. There are civic issues related to canal water, blocked sewerage system and garbage, he said. "But the government does not see the problems which people are facing," he added. "I am only discharging my duties towards my electorate. What is the condition of Sirsa? People are facing so many problems. The drug problem has grown," the MLA claimed. Station House Officer (City), Sirsa, Santosh Kumar, said Mr. Setia was told to write a letter with a pen. "We only told the MLA that he can write a letter with a pen and give it to the chief minister," Mr. Kumar said on the phone. Responding to a question about Mr. Setia's alleged detention by police, Mr. Saini said the opposition MLA had neither been arrested nor taken into custody. The CM described the incident as a "drama". Providing details of funds released for development works in the Sirsa constituency on the opposition MLA's request, Mr. Saini said over ₹94 lakh was released in 2024-25, over $2 crore in 2025-26 and ₹1.65 crore for 28 works in 2026-27. He said a total of ₹4.07 crore had been released for 67 development works over the past three years on the request of the opposition legislator.

headline: Karnataka Congress MLA Nayana Motamma resigns
content: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma on Monday resigned from the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, submitting her resignation at the Speaker’s office in Bengaluru after opposing the Forest Department’s plan to move wild elephants from Belur to Bhadra Tiger Reserve. Motamma, who represents the Mudigere constituency, had on Sunday expressed concern that shifting the elephants could increase human-animal conflict. Congress MLAs T D Rajegowda and H D Thammaiah had also voiced their opposition to the plan. Motamma left Vidhana Soudha after submitting her resignation and did not respond to questions from reporters.

headline: ‘Absolutely the correct thing’: Shashi Tharoor backs Rahul Gandhi’s Palestine remark
content: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Monday endorsed Rahul Gandhi's remarks on the Israel-Palestine conflict, describing his position as "absolutely the correct thing" and saying it was in line with India's long-standing policy on the issue. Tharoor said India had consistently condemned terrorism, including Hamas' October 7 attack on Israeli civilians, while also opposing Israel's military actions in Gaza, which have killed thousands and destroyed homes and livelihoods. "We don't want women, children and innocent civilians to suffer in any conflict. That is why we stand for the rights of both sides," he said during an interaction with PTI Videos. The former Minister of State for External Affairs said India's position was that Palestinians should be able to live with security, dignity and prosperity, while Israel should have safe and defensible borders free from terrorist attacks. He reiterated that India had consistently advocated a two-state solution under which Palestine and Israel could coexist peacefully within secure and defensible borders. "There is no change in India's position. What Rahul Gandhi said is absolutely the correct thing," he said. Tharoor's comments come amid a political controversy over Gandhi's recent remarks at the University of Chicago. Gandhi had supported strong relations with Israel while also calling on India to speak out against the situation in Gaza. CPI(M) veteran and former Keralam Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan had criticised Gandhi, accusing him of hypocrisy on the Palestinian issue. Vijayan alleged that Gandhi's support for stronger ties with Israel and arms purchases from the country contradicted the Congress party's position on Palestine. Tharoor on Congress leaders returning to party Asked about leaders, including Padmaja Venugopal, who had left the Congress and were returning to the party, Tharoor said the decision rested with the party organisation. He said several leaders who had left the Congress under different circumstances might have realised that their decision was wrong. However, he maintained that the party's organisational leadership should handle the matter. Addressing questions about internal differences within the Congress and the UDF government, Tharoor urged party colleagues to prioritise governance and development over political disputes. He said Keralam was facing serious financial challenges, which he attributed to the previous LDF government's "malfeasance and incompetence". The state needed to attract investments, reduce regulatory hurdles and create more opportunities for economic growth, particularly in high-technology industries, he said. Tharoor also highlighted the potential of the silver economy, saying Keralam had several ideas that could contribute to its development. "We cannot do it just like that unless there is cooperation and a relentless focus on the future," he said. The Thiruvananthapuram MP said his discussions in Keralam were focused on the state's development, growth and prosperity. He urged Congress colleagues to support Chief Minister V D Satheesan in working towards these objectives.

headline: India-Nepal train service: PM Modi, Balendra Shah flag off Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu Kamala Express
content: India-Nepal rail connectivity: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Monday flagged off the train service between Ayodhya and Janakpur. The new Ayodhya-Janakpur Saryu Kamala Express is the first direct passenger train service connecting the two destinations across India and Nepal. It will further strengthen connectivity between the neighbouring countries, make travel easier for passengers and promote religious tourism, cultural exchange and trade. India-Nepal rail connectivity: PM Modi, Balendra Shah to flag off Ayodhya-Janakpur Express Shortly — The Indian Express (@IndianExpress) November 23, 2026 This new train service will also establish an important rail link between two destinations deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition - Janakpur Dham (revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita) and Ayodhya (the birthplace of Shri Ram). During its inaugural run, the Ayodhya Dham-Janakpur Dham (Nepal)-Ayodhya Dham Saryu Kamala Express train will operate as train numbers 04295 The inaugural service will reach Janakpur Dham at 10:00 hrs tomorrow. On its return journey, train number 04296 will depart from Janakpur Dham on November 24 and arrive at Ayodhya Dham at 08:10 hrs on November 25. The train's commercial run will be announced soon. Ayodhya-Janakpur Express The Ayodhya-Janakpur Express will cover about 604 km in around 19 hours. It will pass through several important towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. During its journey between Ayodhya and Janakpur, the train will stop at 10 railway stations. These are: Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham. This new train, composed of 17 coaches, will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.

headline: Congress-SP’s 20-minute UP poll meet sign of unease? What top leader said
content: After weeks of bickering over seat-sharing for the high-voltage Assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh, Congress and Samajwadi Party leaders met in Delhi on Monday, but the meeting lasted only 20 minutes. Both parties have picked four leaders for the seat-sharing talks. The Samajwadi Party has chosen veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, MPs Iqra Choudhary and Rajeev Rai, and state party chief Shyam Lal Pal for the negotiations. The Congress has selected AICC in-charge for Uttar Pradesh Rajendra Pal Gautam, state party chief Aradhna Mishra, working president Imran Masood, and MLA Virendra Chaudhary. The meeting was held at Congress MP Pramod Tiwari’s home. The leaders will meet again on Tuesday and the conversation will continue. Sources said the two parties hope to conclude the seat-sharing talks in two-three days. “It was a good meeting. This was the first step. We'll meet again tomorrow. Seats and winnability were discussed,” a source at the meeting said. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Ram Gopal Yadav said the meeting was over, not the conversation. "The meeting was positive. When it is complicated, it takes time," he told reporters. Elections to 403 seats in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly are due early next year. The Congress has submitted a list of 181 seats it wants to contest, but the Akhilesh Yadav-led Samajwadi Party, the main opposition in the state, is reluctant to concede such a large share – 45 per cent of the total seats, citing the Congress’s past performance in the state polls. In the last Assembly polls in 2022, the Congress went solo, contested 399 seats and won just 2, while the Samajwadi Party bagged 111. In 2017, when the two parties contested in an alliance, the Samajwadi Party won 54 seats and the Congress won seven. In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, when the two joined hands, the Samajwadi Party-Congress alliance won 43 out of the state’s 80 parliamentary seats, dealing a major blow to the ruling BJP, which won 72 of the state’s Lok Sabha seats in 2019.

headline: BJP open to Sharad Pawar joining NDA. Here’s what is blocking NCP merger
content: The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) may have publicly shut the door on a merger, but The Indian Express’s conversations with leaders of the BJP and the two NCPs suggest that while the door may be closed, it is not locked. The BJP is open to the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) joining the NDA — and the Mahayuti in Maharashtra — as a separate fourth ally, a move that a section of leaders in the two NCPs see as a possible first step towards an eventual merger. “In the NDA, we believe the more the merrier. If the NCP (SP) decides to associate with the NDA whichever way, we will welcome them. Our equations are cordial. Ideally, we wanted both the groups to merge. But if that's difficult, given the complex power-sharing structure, the NDA will have no problem with getting one more ally (the NCP-SP) on board first,” said a senior BJP minister on the condition of anonymity. “In the Centre and the state, we have a multi-party coalition. We are not averse to managing a coalition. If the NCP (SP) were to come into the NDA as the fourth partner, we don't see any reason why we cannot accommodate them. It is they (NCP-SP) who have to decide,” said a BJP office-bearer. When talk of a merger surfaced after NCP leader Ajit Pawar died in a plane crash on January 28, the BJP did not back the move and the NCP could not proceed without its ally’s green signal. That has since changed. A senior NCP leader said the party had received the BJP’s go-ahead to work out whether, and how, the two parties could come together. “The final decision rests with the two parties,” the leader said. NCP (SP) sources confirmed that their party leadership held several meetings with state BJP leaders before and during Diwali, when Sharad Pawar was in hospital in Pune and later in Mumbai. Publicly, though, the party says there is no proposal. “Since there is no proposal, how can I comment on whether we are joining the Mahayuti or not?” said the party’s working president Supriya Sule, Pawar’s daughter. In the end, whether the merger happens or not depends to a large extent on Pawar, who, BJP leaders claim, pulled the plug once before in 2019 on the NCP’s attempt to join the NDA. What is in it for the BJP? The decision, sources said, is most likely to be made over the next few weeks, with the Winter Session of Parliament providing a window to wrap up negotiations. For the BJP, the immediate interest in bringing the NCP (SP) on board is numbers. In April, the government introduced a legislative package, the centrepiece of which was a Constitution Amendment Bill to enable delimitation and advance the implementation of the women's reservation law. It was bundled together with a Delimitation Bill on the setting up of a Delimitation Commission and a Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill. However, the Constitution Amendment Bill fell short of the two-thirds majority it required to clear the Lok Sabha, defeated 298-230. “The Delimitation Bill will be introduced in the Winter Session of Parliament commencing next month. We are confident of eliciting the requisite two-thirds majority and its smooth passage,” said a senior BJP leader. The NDA’s strength in the Lok Sabha is 320 and 155 in the Rajya Sabha, as per BJP sources. In the Lower House, this number is 40 short of the required 360 for a two-thirds majority in the event that all MPs are present and voting. In the Rajya Sabha, the NDA is six short of the two-thirds mark of 161 at full strength. Though the eight Lok Sabha MPs of the NCP (SP) on their own won’t be enough to bridge the gap in the Lower House, it will help reduce it. Last week, Sule said the party would consider supporting the Constitution Amendment Bill if every state got a uniform 50% increase in seats. But she ruled out joining the NDA. NCP state president and Lok Sabha MP Sunil Tatkare on Sunday welcomed Sule's remarks, but refused to draw inferences from it. "It is a welcome step that she has extended support to the Delimitation Bill. The support to a particular Bill does not necessarily mean that the NCP (SP) will be joining the NDA. There have been instances in the past where several times a Bill was passed unanimously. There is no need to draw political inference from this." Apart from the short term, for the BJP the question ultimately boils down to whether it makes sense to keep sharing power with the NCP, whose strength appears to be waning on the ground, and whether a merger will help prevent that, a leader said. What is blocking a merger? Even with the BJP’s blessing, a merger raises questions that neither of the two NCPs has answered. And that is likely why both have been publicly denying and sidestepping the merger question. The first is who merges into whom. Sunetra Pawar’s party holds the NCP name, symbol, and most of the legislators. So, a merger will mean the NCP (SP) formally joining it. The NCP has a bulk of the MLAs in Maharashtra on its side at 41, against the NCP (SP)’s 10. In the Legislative Council, the NCP is ahead with eight MLCs while Sharad Pawar’s party has three. The only place where the NCP (SP) is ahead is the Lok Sabha, where 8 MPs are with it while the NCP has one. In the Rajya Sabha, however, the NCP has four MPs and Sharad Pawar has one. The second is: who leads? Will Sunetra Pawar, who succeeded her husband as the party leader and Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister, be acceptable to the Sharad Pawar camp? Will she and her son, Rajya Sabha MP Parth Pawar, accept a smaller role to make room for others? What role will Sule play? The third concerns the NCP’s own senior leaders. On November 1, six of them — Tatkare, Praful Patel, Chhagan Bhujbal, Hasan Mushrif, Dilip Walse Patil and Dhananjay Munde — met Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Delhi. Sunetra Pawar and Parth were not told about the meeting, party leaders said. Shah, it is learnt, heard out the leaders and advised them to sort out their differences. The old guard’s complaint, NCP leaders said, is that Parth does not consult them and that Sunetra sides with her son when they raise their concerns. There is unhappiness, a leader said, but no move to change the leadership. A merger could give the second rung a bigger say in how the party is run. What’s at stake for the NCP (SP)? The NCP (SP) has its own reasons to consider joining the Mahayuti and NDA. Out of power, the party has to keep its flock together. Party leaders are wary of what happened to the Shiv Sena (UBT), which lost MPs to Eknath Shinde’s Shiv Sena, and fear further splits. However, the big question that remains is whether Sharad Pawar is willing to join the NDA at all. Only then comes the question of whether the NCP (SP) will go in alone or merge first. Pawar, according to the BJP, has wavered before. Ajit Pawar’s swearing-in as Deputy CM at dawn alongside Devendra Fadnavis as CM in November 2019, and his U-turn days later, is an episode many in the ruling party attribute to the veteran leader’s indecision. Pawar, however, has denied any role in those events. In 2023, he acknowledged the talks with the BJP but added it was his “googly” to “expose” Fadnavis and show how far he could go for power. Joining the NDA will also mean the NCP (SP) leaving the INDIA bloc at the Centre and the Maha Vikas Aghadi in the state. It will reopen power-sharing issues within the Mahayuti too. Ministerial berths will have to be renegotiated and someone, whether the BJP, Shinde’s Shiv Sena or Sunetra Pawar’s NCP, will have to give up something to make room. The Pawar camp at the moment is keeping its cards close to its chest. Recently, Sule distanced the party from MLA Rohit Pawar’s attack on Fadnavis over the probe into Ajit Pawar’s death, saying his remarks were “personal and not endorsed by the party”. Sharad Pawar, meanwhile, was scheduled to attend the Maharashtra Satyashodhak Conference — an anti-caste gathering rooted in the ideology of Jyotirao Phule — in Otur in Pune district on Saturday, but had to cancel after doctors advised him to rest. “His plan to attend the programme in that regard tells us that he has no plans to give up on his original ideology to ally with others,” said a senior leader.

headline: BJP minister Shelar objects to Shiv Sena tearing pages from Sonia Gandhi’s book
content: Days after six spokespersons of the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena tore pages from former Congress president Sonia Gandhi's autobiography, Maharashtra BJP Minister Ashish Shelar on Saturday said he did not approve of the act, adding that he had never torn a book. “Tearing a book is not acceptable to me. I have never torn a book,” Shelar said, in an apparent jibe at the Shiv Sena. He was speaking at the release of senior journalist and author Vijay Chormare’s book, Gatha Bhartiya Nivdunkanchi. Responding to a question about Sonia Gandhi’s autobiography, Shelar spoke about the importance of books and literature. “I feel that the creation of books is a sign of cultural refinement. Whether we agree with the content of a book or not, we should be people who love books. Even if there is a right to protest against the subjects presented in a book, I believe we should adopt a cooperative approach towards the creation of books,” he said. Shelar said people could have objections to the presentation or ideas in a book, but that did not justify tearing it up. He added that books and literature helped society mature and shape individuals. “Hence, tearing a book is not acceptable to me. I have never torn a book, nor have I ever torn up a Prime Minister's decision,” he said. Last week, six Shiv Sena spokespersons held a press conference in Mumbai to protest against what they alleged was an insult to Veer Savarkar and Marathi pride in Sonia Gandhi's autobiography, Belonging: A Journey of Love. The Sena leaders tore pages from the book to register their protest. Shiv Sena spokesperson Sheetal Mhatre said she had spoken to Shelar about his statement. “He told me that he had made a general statement concerning books,” she said. The BJP and the Shiv Sena have been at loggerheads in Maharashtra for some time. Their differences came to the fore during the recent Legislative Council elections, which the Mahayuti lost 3-2. The Shiv Sena had refused to support the BJP candidate, particularly in Pune. The BJP candidate subsequently lost, triggering a war of words between the two alliance partners. The Shiv Sena also faced criticism after Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange-Patil alleged that the BJP had given Rs 500 crore to Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde to be paid to him to silence him. Jarange released an audio clip containing the allegations. Shinde denied receiving or paying any money. Meanwhile, Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal, who was also present at the event, criticised the state government's handling of the investigation into Ajit Pawar's plane crash and questioned the Election Commission's functioning. Referring to NCP state president Sunil Tatkare's statement that he would meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the plane crash investigation, Sapkal asked, “What has been done all these days regarding the investigation? Were they sleeping until now?” Speaking to reporters after the event, Sapkal also questioned the transparency of the electoral process and said there was confusion among the public over the role of the Election Commission of India. “Currently, the situation is such that the electoral process is standing in the dock. However, instead of questioning the functioning of the EC, some people are seen defending it,” he said. On farmer leader Raju Shetti's meeting with the Election Commissioner, Sapkal said, “Raju Shetti is lucky that he went alone and got to meet the Election Commissioner. The reality is that even if we go along with 300 MPs, the Election Commissioner does not meet us.” Sapkal also accused the BJP of seeking to create communal divisions through the proposed delimitation exercise. He said parties in the INDIA alliance were opposing the Bill and that the issue would be discussed at the alliance level. On the possibility of the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) joining hands with the BJP, Sapkal said the party would not do so, adding that MP Supriya Sule had already made its position clear. Asked about the possibility of MLA Rohit Pawar joining the Congress, Sapkal said the NCP (SP) was an ally and that the Congress appreciated his work. However, he said it would not be appropriate to comment on internal decisions or political developments within the party.

headline: Why is India Inc not investing? It wants certainty; the government loves surprises
content: Suppose someone pushed you off a cliff without warning. Later, if the same man invites you to a hilltop picnic, promising glorious views and a feast, would you go? The answer to this is also the answer to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s question to India Inc — why are you not investing enough, creating well-paying jobs and producing high-quality goods? For 33 minutes at last week’s FICCI annual conclave, PM Modi scolded the country’s top industrialists. “I cut corporate tax, yet you did not invest. I raised the income tax threshold, but you did not raise salaries or hire more people. You ran away from agriculture. You produce poor-quality goods for Indian consumers,” he said. Modi is absolutely right about the symptoms of India’s economic disease. Nearly $100bn was given away as tax cuts to corporate India since the cut of 2019. That’s almost what the Union government has spent on education since then, reflecting a misguided belief in ‘trickle-down’ economics, that the tax cuts will spur investment and create jobs. Corporates pocketed the savings and eschewed investment. Their savings (retained profits) rose to 11.2 per cent of GDP in 2023 from 10.5 per cent before the cut, and investment remained stagnant at 12 per cent of GDP. Not enough jobs have been created by private industry over a decade, disillusionment over which brought young people to Jantar Mantar after an alleged paper leak. PM Modi also suffered the ignominy of thousands of unemployed youth forcing out his cabinet minister. He is right to be livid. Who ended up paying for this $100bn corporate bonanza? The middle class. For the first time in India’s recent history, salaried individuals are paying more income tax than companies. The middle class is subsidising the boardroom. Back in 2014, Modi announced a grand Make in India scheme that has cumulatively set aside roughly $30 billion in outlay for corporates to increase manufacturing’s share of GDP to 25 per cent. Twelve years later, forget an increase; the share of manufacturing has come down. One can almost sympathise with Modi’s outburst against the corporates’ “betrayal”. But these supposed corporate betrayals are just the second half of the story of India Inc spurning Modi’s red-carpet invitation to invest. The reasons can be found in the first half of the story, in which corporates were being pushed over the cliff, unaware. When you render the nation’s entire currency stash worthless suddenly and instantly, you create scars that last long. When you declare a nationwide lockdown in four hours, leaving workers and businesses stranded, plans are shelved, payrolls are slashed, and boardrooms learn never to bet big again. When the Enforcement Directorate turns super-aggressive and three times more corporate charges are filed than in the previous tenure, every promoter knows the process is the punishment and looks to flee abroad with their money (Indian corporates now invest three times more money abroad than before). When the top leadership of one of India’s most respected business groups is summoned to the Delhi home of the Home Minister with the Finance Minister in attendance, then the message in this ostensibly suo motu intervention in its internal affairs rings loud in Mumbai — no company is too big to be summoned, and a Delhi sign-off for important decisions is implicitly needed. And then the real elephant in India’s corporate boardrooms: When one business group grows 15 times in market value, triples its market share in ports, enters eight new sectors and corners a significant share of state-owned banks’ loans because it is apparently the “chosen” one, then every promoter comes to believe that the game is rigged, the umpire has a favourite and the smartest bet is to not play at all. Private investment has not vanished; it has been monopolised. Businesses want certainty. Modi loves surprises. The two cannot coexist. Ironically, even the one piece of good news corporate India received arrived as a shock. The corporate tax cut of September 2019 was not announced in the Budget speech, where such decisions belong and where boardrooms wait for them. It came barely two months after the Budget, sprung on an unsuspecting nation at a press conference in Goa. Markets soared for a day. Investment did not follow for a decade. A gift delivered as an ambush is still an ambush. What CFOs learnt that morning was not that taxes had fallen, but that anything could change, anytime, without warning. That irony sums up the fundamental clash at the heart of this government’s economic management. Businesses plan in decades; this government governs by surprises. A steel plant takes five years to build and 25 years to pay back. A refinery, a port, a chip fab, each is a bet that the rules of today will still hold in 2045. When the rulebook can be rewritten overnight, by a midnight address, a four-hour lockdown notice, a summons to a minister’s home or a tax notice bigger than a company’s revenue, no spreadsheet can price the risk. So, the rational promoter does the only rational thing left. She waits. None of this is a secret. The economic advisers and bureaucrats in Modi’s circle know it too. They are simply too scared or servile to tell him. Yet a middle-school student could have told the PM why India Inc is not investing. You cannot push someone off a cliff and then wonder why they decline your picnic invitation. If Modi really wanted FICCI suits to invest, the speech he needed to give would have taken all of two minutes. All he had to do was stand up, promise them that he would never again surprise them or interfere in their affairs, no more overnight bans, no more knocks on the door and no more chosen ones. Instead, he chided, exhorted, lectured and taunted them for 33 minutes. Sermons do not unlock capital. No prizes for guessing how corporate India will respond. It will do what it has done for a decade: Applaud publicly and tighten its wallet privately. The writer is a Member of Parliament from Tamil Nadu & chairman of Data Analytics of Congress
