headline: West Bengal to be renamed 'Paschim Banga'? Proposal to be tabled in Assembly on Dec 9: CM Suvendu
content: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced that a resolution to rename the state as ‘Paschim Banga’ will be moved in the Assembly on December 9. The state Cabinet approved the proposal at a meeting earlier in the day.Speaking to ANI reporters in Kolkata, Adhikari said the resolution would be introduced during the Assembly’s winter session, scheduled from December 4 to 14. He also clarified that ‘Paschim Banga’ would be the state's name in English.“In English, too, West Bengal will be ‘Paschim Banga’. ‘Paschim Banga’—it must be written exactly as is. We are bringing a resolution to the Legislative Assembly on the 9th; following that, it will go to the Government of India and then to Parliament,” he told the news agency.The chief minister said the proposed change was linked to the state's history and its formation in 1947.“This is a matter of history—the history surrounding the formation of West Bengal, which took place in 1947. This change is something that ought to happen. Instead of ‘West Bengal’, it will be ‘Paschim Banga’,” he added.If passed by the state Assembly, the resolution will be sent to the Centre for approval. The renaming will require clearance from the central government and Parliament before it can formally take effect.The announcement follows remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya in October, when he indicated that the state would be renamed.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Stop acting like Baahubali': SC raps Bihar judicial officer for FIR against SP for disobeying directions
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday pulled up a Bihar judicial officer for convicting a police officer over non-compliance with directions to register an FIR. The top court questioned his understanding of contempt law and telling him not to "act like a Baahubali" while exercising judicial powers. The bench also suggested that the judicial officer be sent for training to the National Judicial Academy."Ask your client to stop acting like a 'Bahubali' while exercising judicial powers," Chief Justice Surya Kant said while hearing the judicial officer's plea against a Patna high court order staying his decision.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana criticised district and additional sessions judge-IV, Rohtas at Sasaram, Anil Kumar for convicting the police officer on the same day and treating the non-compliance as an offence committed in the face of the court."We are really surprised at your understanding of law. You must first understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 BNSS and Section 345 CrPC. If someone slaps someone or abuses the court, or refuses to leave the courtroom when directed, that is an offence committed in the face of the court. But if we direct someone to register an FIR and they do not, it does not amount to a crime committed in the face of the court," news agency PTI quoted the bench as saying."Your understanding of law is appalling. You also took such an aggressive stance, called the superintendent and convicted him on the same day," Justice Bagchi said.Questioning the judge's objection to an inspecting judge's intervention, Justice Bagchi said, "Were you within your domain and jurisdiction when you called the district magistrate and superintendent of police, treated their non-appearance as an offence committed in the face of the court and convicted and sentenced him? You also stay your hands. Enough of adventure."On September 29, 2026, Anil Kumar convicted IPS officer Raushan Kumar, then superintendent of police (SP) of Rohtas, for wilfully disobeying court directions to register an FIR against a person who had allegedly given false evidence in a criminal case decided in 2023.The judicial officer imposed a symbolic fine of Rs 1 on the SP and directed Bihar's director general of police (DGP) to enter the court's observations into the officer's service records. He also called on the Union ministry of personnel and training to overhaul the training of IAS and IPS officers to better align them with a democratic setup.The Patna high court had subsequently stayed the order imposing the fine on the SP for contempt of court.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Congress-SP hold 1st round of seat-sharing talks; agreement likely in 2-4 days, say top leaders
content: NEW DELHI: Congress and Samajwadi Party (SP) concluded the first round of seat-sharing talks for 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections on Monday, with the top leaders describing it as "positive". The two parties are likely to finalise their agreement within the next two to four days, leaders of the two parties said, news agency PTI reported.SP general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who is heading the party's talks panel, said both sides had exchanged views and were optimistic about reaching an agreement soon."We expect to complete the alliance within the next two to three days. The second round of talks will be held tomorrow," PTI quoted Yadav as saying.The meeting was held at the residence of Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari in the national capital. Leaders said the talks were progressing in a cordial atmosphere, but did not disclose the number of seats either party is seeking.Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam also described the meeting as positive and said an agreement was close."The meeting went very well and was positive. We will reach an agreement very soon... it is almost finalised," he said."Since the talks are progressing positively, we will not comment on other details, and we will not disclose the seat-sharing details at this stage," he added.Gautam said the two parties would hold another meeting on Tuesday.Uttar Pradesh Congress president Aradhana Misra-Mona also expressed confidence that the arrangement would be finalised soon."I am not talking about numbers. Numbers are not important. ... we will meet again tomorrow, and everything will be finalised," she said, adding that the parties were likely to conclude the process within two to four days.Elections to the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly are due early next year. Chief minister Yogi Adityanath is seeking a third consecutive term, while the SP and Congress are looking to challenge the BJP's dominance in the state.The Congress and SP are working towards a joint contest in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. The Congress is seeking a larger share of seats, citing the outcome of the last Lok Sabha elections and Rahul Gandhi's position as a prominent opposition leader nationally.The SP's negotiation panel is headed by Ram Gopal Yadav and includes party state president Shyam Lal Pal and Lok Sabha MPs Rajiv Rai and Iqra Choudhary. Neither party has disclosed the number of seats being discussed.The two parties contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Ayodhya-Janakpur train, Rs 15,000 crore package, 8 MoUs: Key takeaways from PM Modi and Balen Shah meet
content: NEW DELHI: India and Nepal on Monday signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development, following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.The two leaders also virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal, and jointly inaugurated several development projects during Balen Shah’s two-day state visit to India.At a joint press conference after the talks, Modi said the two countries had taken several important decisions to strengthen bilateral relations.“I am very pleased to welcome Balendra Shah ji to India on his first bilateral visit after becoming the Prime Minister of Nepal. A few months ago, when he addressed the United Nations as the world’s youngest Prime Minister, we got a clear glimpse of his vision. Over the past few hours of our discussions, I have sensed his clear vision and commitment towards Nepal’s future and India-Nepal relations. The historic mandate given to him by the people of Nepal this year reflects the aspirations and hopes of the country’s younger generation. India has always been a partner in the development journey of a strong and prosperous Nepal. In this spirit, today we have taken several important decisions to take our relations to new heights,” PM Modi said.The prime minister also announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development, particularly in the wake of the devastating floods in August.“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. Today, we announce a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees to give fresh impetus to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development. Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities, and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” he said.PM Modi also highlighted the shared religious and cultural ties between the two countries, referring to the launch of the train service connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur.“Lord Ram and Mata Sita are symbols of our shared civilisation and faith. In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said that our pilgrimage sites are incomplete without Nepal, and our Lord Ram is incomplete without Nepal. In 2024, the consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla took place in Ayodhya. This historic occasion gave renewed strength to our shared faith…With the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express train service today, we are giving a new dimension to this sacred bond,” he said.He said India had maintained supplies of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year, and expressed confidence in the future of bilateral ties.“We will together write a golden chapter of India-Nepal relations,” PM Modi said.Saryu-Kamala Express to connect Ayodhya and JanakpurThe Saryu-Kamala Express will connect Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, covering around 604 km in approximately 19 hours. The regular service will operate once a week in each direction from November 28, enabling pilgrims to travel between the two religious destinations without changing trains.The inaugural run on Monday operated as a special train (No. 04295), departing from Ayodhya Dham at 12.30 pm.Eight agreements signed across key sectorsThe eight MoUs exchanged after the delegation-level talks cover satellite communication, policing, forensic sciences, civil service training, healthcare, traditional medicine, sustainable urban development, and livestock and fisheries development.In the space and communication sector, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Nepal’s Ministry of Information and Communication signed an MoU to establish a Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the utilisation of the South Asia Satellite.Two agreements aim to strengthen cooperation in policing and forensic sciences. One provides for academic and research collaboration between the National Forensic Sciences University in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and the Crime Investigation Department of Nepal Police. The other was signed between India’s Rashtriya Raksha University and Nepal’s National Police Academy.For capacity building in public administration, the National Centre for Good Governance, under India’s Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, signed an MoU with Nepal’s Administrative Staff College under the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration. The agreement provides for training programmes for Nepalese civil servants.In healthcare, India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Nepal’s Ministry of Health and Food Safety signed an MoU on cooperation in health and medicine. The two sides also signed a government-to-government agreement on cooperation in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.The remaining two agreements provide for technical cooperation in sustainable urban development and collaboration in livestock and fisheries development.Balen Shah highlights shared ties, climate cooperationAt the joint press conference, Balen Shah described India-Nepal relations as being founded on mutual respect, trust and goodwill.“Ties between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans,” he said.He expressed confidence that the agreements and initiatives announced during the visit would take bilateral relations to a new level, while stressing the need for cooperation on climate change.“I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to build on the strong foundation of this enduring relationship and lay solid pillars for the future. Our Himalayas, the sources of clean water, sustain millions across this region. The pristine rivers flowing from the Himalayas into the Ganga remind us of our future and destiny, underscoring the need to address the challenges of climate change through collective action. Nepal and India have been bound by historical, cultural and civilisational ties since the sacred era of Lord Ram and Mata Janaki,” Balen Shah said.Balen Shah's first bilateral visit to IndiaBalen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day state visit, his first to India since assuming office in March 2026.On Monday, PM Modi received him at Hyderabad House for the bilateral talks. Before the meeting, Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan and paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at the Raj Ghat memorial.Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post on X that the leaders would discuss various aspects of bilateral relations and explore new avenues to deepen cooperation.Jaiswal described the ceremonial welcome as reflecting “the special warmth and enduring friendship between India and Nepal” and Shah’s visit to Raj Ghat as “A tribute to the timeless legacy of Mahatma!”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: 'Astrologer is their ideological guide': MK Stalin takes dig at Vijay's TVK government
content: NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK president MK Stalin on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), alleging that despite declaring social reformer Periyar EV Ramasamy and Dr BR Ambedkar as its ideological leaders, the party was actually following an astrologer.Calling the TVK a "social scourge", Stalin accused the government of reversing Tamil Nadu's development achievements within six months and alleged failures in law and order, drug control, price rise and governance.In a post on X, Stalin said the TVK had adopted Periyar and Ambedkar as ideological figures only in name. "The ruling TVK, having declared Periyar and revolutionary Ambedkar ideological leaders in name only, is operating with an astrologer as its real ideological leader! The TVK, which is ruining Tamil Nadu with the slogan 'Six months, and everything will be destroyed,' is not just a political scourge; it is a social scourge!" he said.Flags law and order, drug menaceTargeting the law and order situation, the DMK leader alleged that people had lost confidence in the police department, citing murders in broad daylight, crimes against women and the growing threat of drug trafficking.He further claimed that major drug consignments seized in Tamil Nadu were being detected by central agencies rather than the state police. Questioning the government's commitment to tackling the drug menace, Stalin alleged that individuals linked to gutkha networks and other controversial activities had been accommodated in the ruling party."Earlier, the competition was between power cuts and intellectual decline. Later, it shifted to drugs and violence. Now, the competition appears to be over who can trouble senior officials in the government, ministers and MLAs," he said.On the economic front, Stalin said the previous DMK government had largely shielded people from the impact of inflation, but prices of essential commodities such as onions, tomatoes and rice had now risen sharply. He also criticised the chief minister for not adequately addressing public concerns.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Gangajal from Triveni, Rudraksh and Chandan from Pashupatinath: PM Modi, Nepal PM exchange gifts
content: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday gifted his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni, while Balen Shah presented him with Rudraksh and Chandan from the sacred Pashupatinath Temple, ahead of their bilateral talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi.The two leaders held discussions to review India-Nepal relations and explore ways to strengthen cooperation across key sectors.The talks are expected to focus on economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. The two sides are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) in areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.Connectivity and energy cooperation are also likely to feature prominently during the visit. The two countries are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay the foundation stones for upcoming initiatives.The visit will also include a Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal. The forum will provide a platform for business representatives from both countries to explore opportunities for collaboration and strengthen commercial ties.PM Modi will host an official luncheon for Shah and his 34-member government delegation.The Nepalese delegation includes finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign Mminister Shishir Khanal, chief advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior officials.Earlier on Monday, Balen Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at his memorial in Raj Ghat, laying a wreath and signing the visitors' book.He also received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with PM Modi in attendance.The two-day state visit provides an opportunity for the two sides to review their bilateral partnership, take stock of ongoing cooperation and explore ways to expand engagement across areas of shared interest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Sachin Pilot calls possible BJP-Akali Dal reunion ‘pure opportunism’, declares ‘AAP govt’s term is over’
content: NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot on Monday termed the reported possibility of a renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab as “pure opportunism”, questioning what had changed since the two parties parted ways.He also criticised the Bhagwant Mann-led Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and said Congress could provide an alternative ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.Addressing the media in Amritsar, Pilot questioned whether the issues that led to the BJP and Akali Dal ending their alliance had been resolved.“Look, the Bharatiya Janata Party has said all those things against the Akali Dal when their mutual agreement ended and for what reasons the alliance between the Akali Dal and BJP had broken. Have all those reasons disappeared?” he asked.Referring to reports of a possible reunion, he said, “The question that arises is: what caused the alliance to break, and what has changed today that you are going to form an alliance again?”Pilot alleged that both parties were struggling to regain their political footing in Punjab after facing rejection in Assembly and Lok Sabha elections.“Now, out of compulsion, they are holding each other's hands right before the elections,” he said.He also referred to the controversy over the three farm laws and allegations concerning drugs, asking the two parties to explain their political differences to voters.“I understand that you were separate for all five years, but what were all the things said regarding the three black laws on drugs? So many people lost their lives in the protest. The Akali Dal and the BJP should answer why they are together today. But I believe this is pure opportunism,” Pilot said.Turning his criticism towards the AAP government, Pilot said its tenure had run its course and claimed voters were looking for a change in Punjab. He also questioned Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's handling of issues in the state.“The Chief Minister has only told jokes and made lighthearted comments over the last five years. Action should be taken seriously on all issues. They haven't done that,” he said.Describing Punjab as “a border state, a very sensitive state”, Pilot said it needed a responsible government. He added that Congress could offer voters an alternative.“The people of Punjab want change, and the Aam Aadmi Party government's term is completely over. The public wants change, and change will happen, along with a better alternative system. If anyone can do it, the Congress party can,” he said.On Congress's preparations for the 2027 polls, Pilot said the State Election Committee would meet on Tuesday and that a screening committee had been formed. Candidates, he said, would be selected on merit, feedback and their prospects of winning.He also expressed confidence that the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance would continue in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections, with seat-sharing talks expected to be finalised soon.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: PM Modi, Nepal PM hold bilateral talks; connectivity, trade, energy on agenda
content: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah arrived at Hyderabad House in New Delhi on Monday for bilateral talks aimed at reviewing ties between the two countries and exploring ways to expand cooperation across key sectors.The discussions are expected to cover the full range of India-Nepal relations, including economic cooperation, trade, investment, transportation, infrastructure, energy and connectivity, as well as regional and international developments of mutual interest.According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the November 22-23 visit is being held at the invitation of Prime Minister Modi. Announcing the visit, the Ministry said the two leaders would review bilateral relations and exchange views on regional and international issues."Prime Minister Modi will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister of Nepal on 23 November 2026 to review the full range of India–Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest," the Ministry stated.The MEA also underlined the historical, cultural and civilisational ties between the two countries, along with their strong people-to-people connections. It noted that bilateral cooperation had expanded across traditional sectors as well as newer areas such as start-ups, technology, innovation and sports."India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports," the Ministry said.Focus on trade, infrastructure and connectivityEconomic cooperation is expected to feature prominently in the discussions, with both sides looking to strengthen engagement in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development.The two countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) in areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.Connectivity and energy cooperation are among the other key areas on the agenda. The two sides are expected to inaugurate completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for new initiatives.The visit will also include a Nepal-India Business Forum, which is aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal and providing business representatives from both countries an opportunity to explore partnerships and strengthen commercial ties.Modi will host an official luncheon for Shah and his 34-member delegation.Balen Shah pays tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj GhatEarlier in the day, Balen Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at his memorial in Raj Ghat, where he laid a wreath and signed the visitors' book.Before this, the Nepalese Prime Minister received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan in the presence of Modi.Balen Shah is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.The two-day state visit provides an opportunity for both countries to review ongoing cooperation and discuss ways to strengthen their bilateral partnership across areas of shared interest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Shashi Tharoor agrees with PM Modi on corporate tax cuts, then takes a jibe
content: NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday backed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's criticism of corporate leaders for failing to pass on the benefits of reduced corporate taxes to employees through higher salaries and increased hiring.However, he also used the Prime Minister's remarks to take digs at the government over the employment situation, regulatory hurdles and corruption.Reacting to the Prime Minister's remarks, Tharoor said PM Modi had a point in arguing that the government had lowered corporate taxes to encourage companies to invest, create jobs and raise salaries, but businesses had not fulfilled their part of the bargain.“I think what the Prime Minister said is a reality. The corporates may have their own defence of it, but his argument, as I understand it, is that the government has lowered taxes to encourage companies to invest more, create more jobs, and raise salaries, and the companies have not kept their share of the bargain,” Tharoor said.He pointed to the difficulties faced by job seekers, particularly fresh graduates, saying the public had repeatedly raised concerns about the lack of employment opportunities.Citing reports of an IIT graduate failing to secure a placement, he said such instances, which were rarely heard of in the past, suggested that the employment environment for college graduates was “rather grim”.Tharoor also called for simpler regulations and improvements in the ease of doing business, while alleging that corruption had worsened and urging the government to pay greater attention to the economy.“The economy requires attention, and if the Prime Minister is pointing fingers at the companies and the companies want to point fingers at government policies, that's something we can watch,” he said.“We do believe there are things the government could be doing better. They could certainly be simplifying regulations; ease of doing business is not a reality. And I'm sorry to say that corruption, according to every businessman I speak to, is much worse than it's ever been,” he added.Taking a swipe at the government's anti-corruption slogan, Tharoor said, “And this is something which, honestly, the Prime Minister had famously said: 'Na khaunga, na khane dunga.' And now we realize he only meant beef.”What PM Modi told corporate leadersTharoor's remarks came after PM Modi, addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting on Thursday, criticised industry leaders for not translating the benefits of corporate tax cuts into higher employee salaries or additional jobs.Recalling that the basic corporate tax rate had been reduced from 30 per cent in 2014 to 22 per cent, the Prime Minister questioned whether companies had increased salaries or expanded their workforce following the tax relief.“I know you will not clap. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough (aapki bhookh itni hai, kitna hi khilao pet bharta hi nahi),” he told the gathering.“Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: 'Modiji, you do it, we will see',” he said.The Prime Minister also cited the income-tax exemption for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh annually, saying the relief had boosted people's purchasing power and consumption. He referred to the government's reduction of GST rates on several products and faster income-tax refunds, which he said had freed up money that would otherwise have remained tied up for months.The remarks came amid fresh demands from the corporate sector for tax concessions in the upcoming Union Budget, with business leaders having submitted their wish list to the finance minister.PM Modi asks industry to suggest reforms, invokes SwadeshiWhile highlighting measures taken by the government to improve the business environment, the Prime Minister urged industry leaders to openly suggest further reforms and assured them that the government was willing to consider their proposals.“I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous govts has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old govt. This is a friendly govt... Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed,” he said.Recalling an interaction with Income Tax Department officials in Gujarat around 2001-02, when he was the chief minister, Modi said he had questioned the approach of treating taxpayers as potential wrongdoers.The Prime Minister also invoked Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance, questioning why industry leaders still needed to be reminded of the importance of promoting indigenous products and building an Atmanirbhar Bharat.“Imagine, 100 years have passed, but in 1930, Gandhi left us with this message, and today, so many years later, I too have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure? Don't listen to me; at least you could have to listen to Gandhi! (Meri mat mano, par Gandhi kih toh mano bhai). He too spoke of Swadeshi before leaving; he too spoke of Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India). And now you have turned 100 years old, yet things remain right where they were ... Spread my message too to every home!” he said.PM Modi also cautioned businesses against taking India's large domestic market for granted, urging them to focus on product quality and ensure their offerings meet international standards.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Yogi Adityanath pens emotional letter to late mother, recalls the day he sought alms from her
content: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath penned an emotional letter to his late mother, Savitri Devi, recalling a deeply personal moment from his life as a monk when he returned home in saffron robes to seek alms from her. The letter, published in the latest edition of ‘Mukhyamantri Pati’, comes days after his 91-year-old mother passed away at her native village in Uttarakhand.Savitri Devi died on Friday morning at her ancestral home in Panchur village in Pauri Garhwal district. Her mortal remains were taken to Namami Gange Ghat, also known as Chandi Ghat, in Haridwar on Saturday for the last rites. Adityanath gave a shoulder to his mother's mortal remains and was seen getting emotional as he paid his final respects.Following her death, the chief minister shared a tribute on X, writing: “There is no shade like a mother’s, no refuge like a mother’s. There is no protection like a mother’s, no love like a mother’s.”In his latest letter, written in Hindi and titled ‘Yogi Ki Pati’, Adityanath dedicated his message to mothers and wrote: “This letter is dedicated to every mother, without whom life would not exist. Without mothers, neither you nor I would be here. No living being would have an existence, and this world itself would not exist. A mother is not merely the one who gives birth; she is the mother of the universe. Even God has a mother.”“Today, once again, my eyes fill with tears as I remember every mother,” Yogi wrote, recalling the blessings of Mata Kaushalya when Lord Ram left for exile and Lord Krishna's journey from the prison in Mathura to Gokul at his mother's wish. “A mother can take the place of anyone, but no one can ever take the place of a mother. A mother's affection is the most beautiful emotion in the world.”The chief minister also recounted an incident from more than three years after he embraced monastic life. Standing outside his home in Panchur in saffron robes, he called out to his mother for alms, as required by the monastic tradition.“Mother, please give me alms,” he recalled saying. His mother, struggling to understand the sight before her, asked: “Son, what have you done to yourself? Is there nothing to eat at home that you have to beg for alms?”Adityanath said he replied: “Mother, renunciation is my duty. A yogi’s hunger can only be satisfied through alms. Mother, I have not come to stay here; I have come to seek alms. Whatever you offer will fulfil my purpose.”In a post on X accompanying the message, Adityanath said the values of Sanatan Dharma were rooted in reverence for mothers. “Some debts can never be repaid. Yes, we can certainly fulfil our duty. Since entering public life, I have been striving to fulfil this duty towards the mothers of our state,” he wrote.“The true mark of respect for every mother would be for every resident of the state to take a pledge today: to become a source of support for a mother without anyone to care for her, to understand the pain of a deprived mother, and to bring a smile to the face of a mother in distress.”The post's accompanying photograph also carried a link to the Uttar Pradesh government's Women and Child Development Department website.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Asia Power Index 2026: US, China, India rank as top 3 powers; PM Modi second to Xi in regional leadership
content: NEW DELHI: India has retained its position among Asia's top three most powerful countries, with its overall power score rising to 40.5 points in 2026, according to a report by the Lowy Institute.The 2026 Asia Power Index also highlights an increasingly contested regional balance, with the gap between the United States and China narrowing largely due to Washington's missteps rather than Beijing's advances. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's regional leadership assessment also improved, with the report placing him second among Asia's regional leaders.Here are the top key findings:India amongest Asia’s top 3 powersThe United States and China continue to dominate Asia's power rankings, but the gap between them has narrowed to its lowest level since the index was launched in 2018. The US leads with 78.9 points, followed by China at 73.6 — a difference of just 5.3 points. The gap in military capability has also narrowed to its smallest recorded level.India ranks third with 40.5 points, followed by Japan with 38.6 points, placing both among Asia's major powers.Modi's regional leadership ranking improvesThe gap between India's and China's overall power narrowed to its lowest level since the Asia Power Index was first published in 2018, although China's power remains 80% higher than India's.Prime Minister Narendra Modi was also ranked Asia's second-most effective regional leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, improving three places.However, perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition declined, with India's muted response to the sinking of an Iranian naval vessel by a US submarine during the Gulf conflict cited as an example of its lower diplomatic profile.India's diplomatic influence holds firm, economic capability sees marginal declineIndia's Diplomatic Influence, however, remained its strongest measure at 70.3 points, slipping only marginally in a year when most countries faltered.India's economic capability score dipped slightly to 26.4 points, with a weakening rupee, changes in the International Monetary Fund's methodology and a nearly $20 billion drop in outbound investment weighing on its relative GDP standing.US stumblesThe United States recorded its steepest-ever decline in diplomatic influence in 2026, with the Trump administration's unilateral foreign policy, trade tariffs and war with Iran eroding its standing across Asia. Washington's strained ties with international institutions, along with President Donald Trump's remarks on arms sales to Taiwan and military exercises with South Korea, further weakened regional confidence in US leadership.The US Diplomatic Influence score fell by six points to 76.7, marking the fourth consecutive year of decline and the biggest single-year drop in the measure since the Asia Power Index was launched in 2018.The 2026 Asia Power Index evaluates 27 countries and territories across 131 indicators covering eight measures of power, including economic and military capability, resilience, diplomatic influence and economic relationships.Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Tearing books is unacceptable, says BJP minister Ashish Shelar
content: Pune: State cabinet minister and senior BJP leader Ashish Shelar on Sunday said tearing books was unacceptable to him. His remarks came against the backdrop of Shiv Sena members tearing copies of senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.Speaking at a book launch event in Pune, Shelar said, without naming anyone, “Tearing books is not at all acceptable to me. I have never torn a book in my life.”“Readers may have different views, which may inspire some and distress others. Books enrich society. Reading is essential to shaping an individual,” he added.The state cultural affairs minister said citizens had the right to express positive or negative opinions about a book and stage protests over its content. However, he maintained that tearing books was unacceptable.The controversy erupted after members of the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena tore copies of Sonia Gandhi’s book to protest alleged objectionable remarks about freedom fighter VD Savarkar.During the protest, Sena leader Shaina NC inadvertently tore a photograph of Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray while tearing pages of the book. The incident triggered protests by the Opposition. headline: How CM Yogi Adityanath changed employment ecosystem in Uttar Pradesh
content: LUCKNOW: The ambition of the Yogi government is not merely to provide jobs, but to transform Uttar Pradesh into an economy where government recruitment, private enterprise, manufacturing and entrepreneurship together drive prosperity and employment.Rewriting Uttar Pradesh's employment storyFor decades, Uttar Pradesh faced one of the country's most demanding development challenges: providing livelihoods to an enormous and growing young population. With limited industrial opportunities and too few jobs close to home, millions of people left their villages and towns for Delhi, Mumbai, Gujarat and other industrial centres.Migration became a familiar part of family life in many districts, particularly in the eastern and central parts of the state. Households often depended on remittances sent from distant cities, and young people spent their most productive years far from their families.Changing this reality required more than filling vacancies in government departments. It demanded a transformation of the state's economic environment. Investment, infrastructure, manufacturing, entrepreneurship and skill development all had to work together as engines of employment, so that a young person could find a worthwhile opportunity without leaving the state.Since 2017, the Yogi Adityanath government has pursued this approach on several fronts at once. Its employment figures point to an expanding ecosystem of public-sector recruitment, private enterprise, MSMEs and industrial investment.The government reports that approximately 9.5 lakh young people have received government jobs since 2017. In addition, more than four crore employment opportunities have been generated through MSMEs and private entrepreneurship.These two figures represent the pillars of the state's strategy: expanding public employment while creating opportunities across the wider private economy.9.5 lakh government jobs: Recruitment through transparencyOne of the achievements the government highlights most is the appointment of approximately 9.5 lakh people to government posts since 2017. For a state with Uttar Pradesh's population and its competitive examination culture, recruitment at this scale matters.Government employment remains among the most sought-after career paths for young people, and millions of aspirants prepare for it every year.These appointments span police, education, health, medical education, revenue, technical services and other departments. According to government figures, police recruitment alone accounts for more than 2.25 lakh appointments, while teacher recruitment has crossed 1.5 lakh.Together, these appointments have strengthened the frontline machinery of law enforcement, schooling and public services.The government has emphasised transparency, merit-based selection and time-bound recruitment. Its stated objective has been to move away from the irregularities and delays that, in earlier years, had undermined the confidence of young aspirants.For candidates who spend years preparing, a predictable and credible process is itself a form of public service.Recruitment has also continued beyond the initial large-scale drives. The chief minister has set a target of providing one lakh additional government jobs by January 26, 2027.Processes are underway for thousands of police and Home Guard positions, alongside vacancies in other departments. The distribution of appointment letters to 1,146 junior assistants in the Revenue Department on November 11, 2026, reflects this continuing momentum.MSMEs and private entrepreneurship: Four crore employment opportunitiesGovernment employment is only one part of Uttar Pradesh's changing employment story. No government can employ more than a fraction of its young citizens directly. The larger transformation is therefore taking place through micro, small and medium enterprises and private entrepreneurship.Uttar Pradesh has nearly 96 lakh MSME units, making it one of India's largest MSME ecosystems. These enterprises support employment across textiles, leather, carpets, handicrafts, food processing, engineering, metal products and many other sectors.Many are family-run or located in small towns and villages, so they provide livelihoods where large factories are rarely found.The government estimates that MSMEs and private entrepreneurship have generated more than four crore employment opportunities.This figure shows the importance of enterprises that provide livelihoods beyond formal government recruitment, particularly in smaller towns and rural areas, where a local workshop, a processing unit or a small manufacturing firm can change the economic prospects of an entire neighbourhood.To strengthen this sector, the Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy 2022 offers eligible enterprises capital subsidies of up to 25%, subject to a ceiling of Rs 4 crore. Interest subsidies, stamp-duty exemptions and other incentives seek to encourage investment, modernisation and expansion.Special provisions for Purvanchal and Bundelkhand aim to promote entrepreneurship in relatively less-developed regions, so that growth is not concentrated in a few established industrial pockets.Digital platforms such as MSME 1-Connect are also intended to simplify access to government schemes, financial assistance and business support.For a first-generation entrepreneur, easier access to information and credit can make the difference between an idea that stays on paper and a business that hires its first workers.ODOP: Traditional skills become modern enterprisesThe One District One Product (ODOP) initiative, launched in January 2018, has emerged as a distinctive pillar of the government's employment strategy. It rests on a simple observation: nearly every district in Uttar Pradesh has a traditional product, craft or skill that generations of artisans have preserved, but many of these producers lacked the design, technology and market access to turn their skills into stable incomes.ODOP identifies the signature product of each district and gives producers support in design, technology, branding, packaging, finance and marketing.Banarasi silk, Lucknow Chikankari, Bhadohi carpets, Moradabad brassware, Kannauj perfumes, Saharanpur woodcraft, Firozabad glassware and Agra leather products are among the products receiving focused attention.By connecting artisans and traditional manufacturers with larger domestic and international markets, ODOP has sought to turn inherited skills into commercially viable enterprises. According to Invest UP, ODOP products generated approximately Rs 93,000 crore in exports in 2024.The next phase, ODOP 2.0, places greater emphasis on quality, modern technology, e-commerce and international competitiveness.The initiative's larger contribution lies in strengthening local production networks. When a district's signature product finds new buyers, the benefits reach artisans, suppliers, transporters, packaging units and small traders, creating opportunities for workers and entrepreneurs within their own districts rather than in distant cities.Investment and industrialisation: Expanding the employment baseInfrastructure development has been central to the state's efforts to attract investment and create new employment centres. Expressways, airports, industrial corridors and logistics facilities have improved connectivity and made Uttar Pradesh more attractive for manufacturing and services.Good roads, reliable logistics and access to markets are often what decide whether a company sets up a factory in a state.The state has attracted investment proposals worth approximately Rs 50 lakh crore through investor summits and other initiatives.Ground Breaking Ceremonies have translated a substantial part of this pipeline into projects at various stages of implementation, which is the step that matters most for employment, since proposals create jobs only when they become operating units.Several clusters illustrate the direction of this expansion. Electronics and mobile-phone manufacturing in Noida and Greater Noida, the Defence Industrial Corridor across six nodes, and the emerging industrial region around the Noida International Airport are creating opportunities in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, aviation and allied services.Such industries also generate secondary employment in transport, construction, hospitality and ancillary supply chains.The government is also promoting investment beyond established industrial centres, with particular attention to Bundelkhand and Purvanchal. The aim is more balanced regional development, so that young people in every part of the state have access to opportunity.Skills and employment connectivityJobs and investment alone are not enough unless young people have the skills employers want. The government has therefore strengthened vocational training, apprenticeship programmes, employment fairs and industry-linked skill development.The Rojgaar Sangam portal serves as a platform connecting jobseekers with private-sector vacancies, employers, campus placements, employment fairs and career guidance. By bringing both sides of the labour market onto one platform, it aims to reduce the gap between those looking for work and those looking for workers.Internship initiatives under the PM and CM programmes are also intended to give young people practical experience and improve their employability. Exposure to real workplaces helps graduates build confidence and professional skills that classroom learning alone cannot provide.The objective throughout is to bridge the gap between education and industry requirements, so that the state's expanding economy has access to a skilled workforce.From migration to opportunityThe significance of Uttar Pradesh's employment transformation lies in the combination of government recruitment and private-sector expansion. The 9.5 lakh government appointments represent one dimension; the more than four crore employment opportunities attributed to MSMEs and private entrepreneurship represent the much larger livelihood-generating ecosystem.Both are needed: public jobs offer security and stability, while enterprise offers scale and dynamism.The challenge ahead is to ensure that investment commitments become operational projects, that employment opportunities translate into sustainable jobs, and that workers receive better incomes and working conditions. Numbers on paper matter less than the quality and durability of the livelihoods behind them.Nevertheless, the policy direction marks an important shift. Uttar Pradesh is seeking to move beyond an economy dependent on migration towards one capable of generating opportunities within its own districts.For a young person in eastern Uttar Pradesh, an artisan in the west or an aspiring entrepreneur in Bundelkhand, the larger promise is that employment and enterprise should increasingly be possible closer to home.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. headline: ‘Don’t act like Robin Hood or Bahubali’: SC rebukes Bihar judge for convicting SP
content: The Supreme Court on Monday cautioned a Bihar judicial officer against acting like “Robin Hood” or a “Bahubali”, reminding him that a judge must know the limits of his jurisdiction, as it expressed dismay over the judge convicting a superintendent of police (SP) for failing to comply with his direction to register an FIR.“Enough of adventure. Go to the National Judicial Academy and have training. You don’t have to become Robin Hood…Do you want to become a Bahubali (strongman)?... You must understand your limits and jurisdiction as a judge,” a bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said.The bench questioned sessions judge Anil Kumar’s decision to invoke the procedure for offences committed in the face of the court, pointing out that an official’s failure to comply with a judicial direction to register an FIR could not be treated as contempt committed in the courtroom.“We are really surprised at your understanding of the law concerning a violation or a crime committed on the face of the court. You first must understand the scope and ambit of Section 384 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Section 345 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC),” it observed.Explaining the distinction, the court said an offence committed in the face of the court would include an act such as slapping someone, abusing the court or refusing to leave the courtroom despite being directed to do so. However, failure to register an FIR despite a court direction did not fall within that category.“But if we say that X must register an FIR and X does not register an FIR, it does not amount to a crime committed on the face of the court,” the bench said, describing the judicial officer’s understanding of the law as “appalling”.The top court was hearing a challenge to proceedings the sessions judge had initiated against the Rohtas SP over repeated delays in complying with his directions. Kumar had summoned the police officer, treated the non-compliance as an offence committed in the face of the court, convicted him and imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh.The case arose from a September 2025 sessions court order directing the police to register an FIR against the victim and the informant in a criminal matter, which the police complied with nearly 10 months later, in July 2026. Kumar also noted other instances of delayed compliance, including a belated response to a demand for an explanation and failure to submit a status report on a recommendation for disciplinary action against the SP.Kumar approached the top court against an October 8 order of the Patna High Court, which termed the situation “peculiar” and “unprecedented” and observed that the sessions judge was required to maintain “procedural integrity” since the underlying judgment, including its direction to register an FIR, was already under challenge before it. The high court also sought the complete records of the criminal proceedings initiated against the SP and directed that the matter should not be precipitated pending an early hearing of the appeal, scheduled for November 25.While acknowledging the judicial officer’s intention to secure compliance with court orders, the Supreme Court made it clear that the desire to do justice could not justify bypassing the procedure prescribed by law.“We understand your sentiments. We appreciate your effort to reach out and do justice. But as we are governed by certain procedural constraints and discipline, we cannot forget that,” it told Kumar’s counsel.The bench also questioned Kumar’s objection to an inspecting judge summoning him in an administrative capacity, asking whether he had himself remained within his jurisdiction when he called upon the district magistrate and the SP to appear personally and then treated their non-appearance as an offence warranting conviction and sentence.“Were you within your domain and jurisdiction to exercise this?” asked the bench, adding that the matter could have been left to the high court if the judicial officer believed the SP’s conduct amounted to criminal contempt.The bench also referred to the training imparted at the National Judicial Academy, stressing that judicial officers must be conscious of the legal boundaries of their authority and cannot assume powers beyond what the law permits.Reiterating that judicial officers must remain mindful of the legal boundaries of their authority and undergo refresher training at the National Judicial Academy, the Supreme Court disposed of the matter while requesting the Patna High Court to consider Kumar’s response and any apology he may submit “considerately”.

headline: West Bengal to be renamed ‘Paschim Banga’; proposal to be tabled in assembly on December 9: CM Suvendu
content: A proposal to rename West Bengal as 'Paschim Banga' will be tabled in the assembly during the next session, beginning on December 4, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Monday.The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Adhikari."The proposal to rename West Bengal as 'Paschim Banga' will be tabled in the House on December 9," he said after the meeting.ALSO READ: Bengal to be renamed, says BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya: ‘How many times must I say?’Once the proposal is passed by the assembly, it will be sent to the Centre for its approval, he said.ALSO READ: Poll body must set the record straight on SSR delay in West BengalThe winter session of the assembly will be held from December 4 to 14.

headline: Balen Shah invites PM Modi to Nepal, urges Indians to visit Pashupatinath, other religious sites
content: Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah, who is in India on a two-day official visit, invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi to his country on Monday. Shah also encouraged Indians to visit Pashupatinath and other religious and tourist destinations in Nepal, as he said that the relationship between the two neighbouring nations remains “as strong as the Himalayas”.Track live updates on Balen Shah's India visitThe two leaders held bilateral talks at Hyderabad House in New Delhi to review India-Nepal relations and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation across key sectors. Shah arrived in India on Sunday for a two-day visit between November 22 to 23.During the Nepalese leader's visit to India, at least eight Memorandums of Understanding were signed to expand bilateral cooperation across sectors, including satellite technology, governance, healthcare, urban development and traditional medicine. PM Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of his Nepalese counterpart and his 34-member government delegation.Modi and Shah also flagged off the Saryu Kamala Express, a new train service connecting Ayodhya Dham in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, a move aimed at strengthening cross-border connectivity and religious tourism between India and Nepal.The new train service is expected to facilitate pilgrim movement between Ayodhya and Janakpur, both of which hold significant religious importance.Ayodhya is associated with Lord Ram, while Janakpur is revered as the birthplace of Goddess Janaki. Improved rail access between the two destinations could encourage religious tourism and provide a more convenient travel option for devotees from both countries.Also read: Modi, Balen Shah flag off Ayodhya-Janaki Dham train to boost India-Nepal tiesShah is accompanied by finance minister Swarnim Wagle, foreign minister Shishir Khanal, chief advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.Earlier in the day, Shah laid a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial in Raj Ghat andd paid tribute to the Father of the Nation. , Mahatma Gandhi, by laying a wreath at his memorial in Raj Ghat, as part of his state visit to India.The Nepal PM also signed the guestbook at the memorial site after he paid a floral tribute to the Father of the Nation.Prior to this, PM Shah received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with Prime Minister Modi in attendance.The two-day State visit is expected to provide an opportunity for both sides to take stock of their bilateral partnership, review ongoing cooperation and explore ways to expand engagement across areas of shared interest.

headline: India, Nepal sign 8 MoUs from space to security as Modi hosts Balen Shah
