headline: Keeping up with UP | Why Chirag Paswan’s UP plan matters to BJP’s 2027 non-Jatav Dalit maths
content: As the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) prepares to seek a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh’s 2027 state assembly elections, its strategy appears to rely on a familiar political formula: accommodating small regional partners while welcoming tactical contenders capable of fragmenting the Opposition votes.The Bihar-based Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) president, Chirag Paswan, stepped up earlier this month, saying his party would contest the Uttar Pradesh elections to be held early next year.For the record, Chirag said his party hadn’t started negotiations to join the BJP-led alliance in the state and was ready to contest all 403 seats if there was no consensus on the seat-sharing arrangement.His party leaders have focused on parts of central and eastern UP for months to make inroads into the Pasi- and Paswan-dominated constituencies and counter the Samajwadi Party-led Opposition alliance’s ‘PDA’ (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) narrative. But nothing suggests Chirag Pawan, who recently inaugurated the party’s state office in Lucknow, had built a booth-level organisation in the state that would be needed to contest elections on their own.It is in this context that the LJP’s entry is seen less as a bid to establish an independent third force and more as an intervention that could split the Opposition’s Dalit vote bank in an election that is shaping up as a direct bipolar contest between the BJP-led NDA and the SP-Congress combine, with the smaller regional players increasingly emerging as potential tactical assets on the margins.To be sure, the LJP is already the fifth NDA ally to signal plans to contest the state polls—joining Om Prakash Rajbhar’s Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party, Sanjay Nishad’s Nishad Party, Anupriya Patel’s Apna Dal (Sonelal) and Jayant Chaudhary’s Rashtriya Lok Dal, all of whom have thrown around hefty seat demands in the ongoing, inconclusive negotiations with the BJP.The non-Jatav arithmeticAt the heart of Paswan’s Uttar Pradesh pitch is a bid to woo non-Jatav Dalit voters, specifically the Pasi sub-caste, along with the younger Gen Z electors. He will be expected to peel the Pasi-Paswan votes away from the SP-Congress alliance, which has been consolidating backward-Dalit votes through its PDA strategy.Pasis account for roughly 9% of Uttar Pradesh’s 21% Scheduled Caste electorate. The core Jatav base among SC’s has largely stayed with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) but as Mayawati’s party steadily lost ground over the past decade, non-Jatav Dalits have emerged as a significant swing bloc. Pasis and other sub-groups have fractured across rival camps.The shift of Pasi and Paswan votes to the SP-Congress alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections led to the NDA’s defeat in several constituencies in central and eastern UP, including Mohanlalganj, Dhaurhara, Sitapur, Kheri, Kaushambi, Pratapgarh, Sultanpur, Ambedkar Nagar, Shravasti and most visibly in Faizabad (Ayodhya) where SP candidate Awadhesh Prasad won.Paswan’s outreach, built around campaigns such as ‘Bol Yuva’, Pasi-Paswan Shaurya Samman and Dalit chaupals, aims to reverse this drift toward the Opposition.Whether Paswan can deliver without an entrenched organisational network in Uttar Pradesh remains an open question. This is where the BJP’s organisational machinery could provide crucial backing, much as it has for smaller partners in Bihar. Even so, in a tightly contested election where every fraction of a percentage point counts, both Pasi and younger electors will seek answers to local bread-and-butter issues they have been posing to the state’s double-engine government.This isn’t the first time the LJP has decided to test the waters in Uttar Pradesh. In previous attempts, it could never cross one per cent of the total vote. In 2022, the party contested 21 seats on its own, lost every deposit and polled just 12,247 votes (0.01% vote share).Ram Vilas Paswan’s forays too had failedIn 1987, when Vishwanath Pratap Singh floated the Jan Morcha after breaking with Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s Congress, he saw in Ram Vilas Paswan the potential to become India’s first Dalit prime minister.Though that office eluded him, the senior Paswan went on to serve as a Union cabinet minister under six prime ministers -- VP Singh, HD Deve Gowda, IK Gujral, Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Manmohan Singh and Narendra Modi -- and earned a reputation as a political bellwether for his ability to anticipate electoral winners.But he could never expand his party’s base in Uttar Pradesh, despite making several forays in the 1980s and early 1990s. He had formed a Dalit Sena to penetrate the Dalit vote bank, especially in western UP.In 1985, Ram Vilas Paswan contested a Lok Sabha by-election from the reserved constituency of Bijnor in western UP as a Lok Dal candidate against Meira Kumar, daughter of deputy prime minister Jagjivan Ram, and Mayawati of the fledgling Bahujan Samaj Party, founded in 1984. Meira Kumar won the seat, defeating Ram Vilas Paswan by just over 5,000 votes. Mayawati, who had contested as an independent, came third.Paswan tried again in 2002, just two years after he broke away from the Janata Dal and formed the Lok Janshakti Party in 2000. The LJP contested 18 seats, won one seat in Jaunpur and lost four seats by a narrow margin. It polled its highest vote share: 0.59%. Thereafter, the party contested the 2007 and 2012 assembly polls but gradually became redundant in state politics as the SP and BSP had by then arrived on the scene in a big way.Ram Vilas Paswan died in 2020, triggering a succession battle between Chirag and his uncle, Pashupati Kumar Paswan, and a split in June 2021. For the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, BJP chose Chirag over his uncle and helped him back on his feet.In the run-up to the campaign, Prime Minister Narendra Modi described Chirag Paswan as ‘like my son, the future of Bihar.’ Chirag responded, declaring himself PM Modi’s Hanuman to display his loyalty and recalling the bond between the prime minister and his late father.“Their relationship was very special. Prime Minister Narendra Modi always gave my father love, respect and honour. He now extends the same affection to me. I am inseparable from Prime Minister Modi,” he said. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Chirag’s party won all five Lok Sabha seats it was allocated.In Bihar, the LJP proved adept at weaning many Dalit voters away from the RJD-Congress alliance. Whether Chirag Paswan can replicate that formula in Uttar Pradesh’s far more complex caste matrix remains an open question. For the BJP, however, LJP’s presence matters less for building an enduring organisation in Uttar Pradesh than for blunting the Opposition’s margins.

headline: Modi, Balen Shah flag off Ayodhya-Janaki Dham train to boost India-Nepal ties
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah on Monday flagged off the Saryu Kamala Express, a new train service connecting Ayodhya Dham in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, in a move aimed at strengthening cross-border connectivity and religious tourism between the two neighbouring countries.The launch followed a meeting between Modi and Shah, who is on a visit to India, and marked another step towards deepening bilateral cooperation through improved transport infrastructure.The train will connect important destinations across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Nepal, with stoppages at Gorakhpur, Basti, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Madhubani and Jaynagar. The service is expected to make travel more convenient for passengers, particularly devotees visiting the two religious destinations associated with Lord Ram and Goddess Janaki. Addressing the launch programme at Ayodhya Cantt railway station, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath said the service would revive the ancient religious and cultural ties between Ayodhya and Janakpur. "The launch of this rail service will enable devotees from Nepal to directly visit Ram Lalla, while devotees from India will be able to visit Janakpur Dham and seek the blessings of Mata Janaki," Adityanath said.Describing the train as a "sacred and mythological confluence of two cultures", the chief minister said the connection between Ayodhya and Mithila was rooted in centuries-old traditions. He said the relationship between India and Nepal was built on shared faith, affection, rivers and families, commonly described as the 'roti-beti' relationship.Recalling the traditional association between Awadh and Mithila, Adityanath said people in Ayodhya continued to regard Janakpur as their relatives' home, while people in Mithila referred to Lord Ram as 'Pahun', or son-in-law.The chief minister also referred to the traditional celebrations of Vivah Panchami, which commemorates the marriage of Lord Ram and Goddess Janaki. He said the wedding procession of King Dasharath to Janakpur and the journey of Ram and Lakshman to Mithila with Maharishi Vishwamitra continued to be celebrated as living traditions.Adityanath thanked Modi, Shah and Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw for the initiative, saying it reflected the Centre's vision of combining heritage with development.Religious tourism and regional connectivityThe new train service is expected to facilitate pilgrim movement between Ayodhya and Janakpur, both of which hold significant religious importance.Ayodhya is associated with Lord Ram, while Janakpur is revered as the birthplace of Goddess Janaki. Improved rail access between the two destinations could encourage religious tourism and provide a more convenient travel option for devotees from both countries.The service is also expected to benefit passengers travelling for family visits and other purposes across the connected regions. Increased movement could provide opportunities for local businesses, including hotels, shops and transport operators, although the economic impact will depend on passenger demand.Also Read I Ayodhya-Janakpur direct rail service to strengthen India-Nepal tiesAdityanath highlighted several other religious and cultural links between India and Nepal, including the association between the Pashupatinath temple in Nepal and the Kashi Vishwanath temple in Varanasi.He also referred to the tradition of offering khichdi sent from Nepal at the Gorakhnath temple in Gorakhpur on Makar Sankranti and the annual pilgrimage from Nepal to the Devipatan Shaktipeeth in Uttar Pradesh during Chaitra Navratri.The chief minister further highlighted the shared Buddhist heritage of the two countries, noting that Lord Buddha was born in Lumbini in Nepal, while several important milestones of his life and teachings were associated with places in Uttar Pradesh, including Sarnath, Shravasti and Kushinagar.India-Nepal rail cooperationThe Ayodhya Dham-Jan akpur Dham service is part of broader efforts to expand railway connectivity between India and Nepal.Several rail projects are aimed at improving cross-border passenger movement and facilitating commercial activity. These include the Jaynagar-Bijalpura-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar rail links, which are progressing in stages.The proposed Raxaul-Kathmandu railway line is also part of the wider plan to strengthen connectivity between the two countries.Also Read I PM Modi, Nepal’s Balen Shah to hold talks today, inaugurate Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link, other key projectsAlongside infrastructure development, India has been supporting capacity building for Nepal's railway operations. Nepal Railway officers and staff have received training in various aspects of train operations at Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya in Vadodara.The launch of the Saryu Kamala Express adds to these efforts by connecting important religious and cultural destinations across the border.Adityanath said the service would give fresh impetus to the longstanding friendship between India and Nepal and allow devotees from both countries to reconnect with their shared heritage.

headline: ‘Every dose a step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer’: PM Modi on 1 crore HPV vaccine doses milestone
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday hailed the administration of over one crore doses under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign, describing it as a significant milestone in India's preventive healthcare efforts and emphasising the importance of protecting adolescent girls against cervical cancer.In a post on X, PM Modi said, "A significant milestone in our journey towards preventive healthcare. Every dose is a step towards protecting girls from cervical cancer and ensuring a healthier future for them. I commend all the stakeholders whose efforts have ensured this remarkable feat."https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2124707476616675534According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India has administered more than one crore doses of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months since the launch of the nationwide campaign in February 2026.The campaign provides free, safe and voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination, with parental consent, to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities. The initiative aims to protect adolescent girls against HPV infections that can cause cervical cancer.The campaign has achieved nearly 87 per cent cumulative coverage against the identified annual target cohort of approximately 1.2 crore girls, based on the Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 population estimates.The Ministry said that reaching the one crore-dose milestone within nine months reflects the scale and momentum of the initiative, supported by coordinated efforts of States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, frontline workers, teachers, parents and local communities.Meanwhile, Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda also welcomed the achievement, highlighting the contribution of States and healthcare workers in expanding vaccination coverage.In a post on X on Saturday, Nadda wrote, "In less than nine months since its launch by Hon’ble PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, the National HPV Vaccination Campaign has achieved this historic milestone in protecting India’s daughters against cervical cancer."Congratulations to Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar for achieving 100% coverage, with 12 States surpassing 80%. This remarkable progress reflects the collective commitment of States/UTs, healthcare professionals, frontline health workers and parents across the country. With free, safe and effective single-dose HPV vaccination available for eligible 14-year-old girls through Government health facilities and U-WIN, India is moving closer to a future free from cervical cancer," the post read.Six States -- Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar -- have achieved 100 per cent coverage of their identified target populations under the campaign.Among other high-performing States, Assam has recorded 95.63 per cent coverage, followed by Telangana at 95.28 per cent, Karnataka at 93.16 per cent and Uttarakhand at 90.17 per cent.Chhattisgarh has recorded 86.21 per cent coverage, while Rajasthan has achieved 85.23 per cent. Kerala has reported 77.02 per cent coverage, Tamil Nadu 76.12 per cent, Odisha 74.90 per cent and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 72.99 per cent.In terms of absolute numbers, Uttar Pradesh leads the country with more than 29.33 lakh 14-year-old girls vaccinated, followed by Bihar with over 13.70 lakh and Gujarat with over 7.75 lakh girls vaccinated.The Ministry said that progress across States with diverse geographical, demographic and socioeconomic conditions highlights the extensive reach of the campaign and the effectiveness of locally adapted implementation strategies.

headline: Delhi court issues non-bailable warrant against Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
content: A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 criminal defamation case, after observing that he failed to appear before it despite a bailable warrant having already been issued against him.Judicial magistrate first class Aman Rais Khan of Saket courts issued the warrant after noting that neither Rathee nor any counsel representing him appeared during the proceedings. The court has fixed December 3 as the next date of hearing.The case stems from a criminal defamation complaint filed by Vikas Sanskrityayan over a video titled “BJP IT Cell Part II”, which Rathee produced and uploaded on his YouTube channel in May 2018.In the video, Rathee had alleged that members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)'s IT Cell had attempted to bribe Sanskrityayan to malign his reputation. Sanskrityayan subsequently approached the court, alleging that the claims were false, malicious and intended to damage his reputation.The video had attracted widespread attention after it was shared on social media by former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal. Sanskrityayan had initiated defamation proceedings against both Rathee and Kejriwal. Kejriwal later admitted before the court that sharing the video was a mistake, following which separate proceedings against him ensued. The complaint against Rathee, as the creator and publisher of the video, continued.The proceedings against Rathee have been pending for several years, with the court facing difficulty in securing his appearance. The court had first issued notices to him in July 2019.The latest escalation by the court came after the judge noted that Rathee failed to respond to the summons and the bailable warrant issued against him in the case.On October 12, the court had issued fresh summons after the complainant sought expedited proceedings in the matter. At the time, the complainant's counsel, advocate Samaksh Sharma, had informed the court that Rathee, who ordinarily resides in Germany, was in India to attend a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest and provided an address in Sector 56, Gurugram, where he was believed to be staying.During the last hearing in the matter, the court issued a bailable warrant after noting that the earlier warrant had been sent to an incorrect address in Austria instead of Rathee's Gurugram residence. The complainant's counsel had also informed the court that Rathee had left India and was residing overseas.

headline: Congress, Samajwadi Party leaders say UP seat-sharing talks ‘cordial’, final announcement in 2-3 days
content: The long-awaited seat-sharing negotiations between the Samajwadi Party and the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections formally began in Delhi on Monday with a brief but “positive” first-round meeting between the four-member panels of both parties.The talks, held in a “cordial atmosphere”, focused on finalising the agenda and key points for seat allocation across the state’s 403 Assembly constituencies. Leaders from both sides stressed mutual respect and a shared commitment to a workable formula based primarily on winnability rather than rigid numbers.Samajwadi Party Rajya Sabha MP and national general secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, who heads the SP panel, said after the meeting, "The meeting took place in a very cordial atmosphere. We listened to each other's points of view, and we will soon finalise this alliance and inform you about it. We will complete the process within the next two to three days. The next meeting will take place tomorrow."Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam echoed the positive tone, "Both parties are in agreement, they trust each other, and they will manage things jointly. This is nearly settled, and an agreement will be reached in a respectful manner. It will happen very soon," he said.Congress MP Pramod Tiwari, whose residence is understood to be the venue for the discussions, added that both parties were examining constituency-wise strengths and data. "Everyone has their own figures and facts based on their respective strengths. The meeting will continue today and, if required, we will meet again tomorrow. We will work out a formula and arrive at a decision," he said.Also Read: 2027 Uttar Pradesh polls: Samajwadi Party, Congress form four-member panels each for seat-sharing talksUP Congress President Aradhana Misra (Mona) also said the meeting was held on a very positive note. "I am confident that we will finalise everything within the next two to four days. I am not talking about numbers. Numbers are not important. We have reached a consensus on this between the two of us, and as I said, we will meet again tomorrow, and everything will be finalised,” she said.The negotiating panelThe Samajwadi Party panel is headed by Ram Gopal Yadav. The other members are UP state president Shyam Lal Pal, Ghosi Lok Sabha MP Rajiv Rai, and Kairana Lok Sabha MP Iqra Chaudhary (Iqra Hasan).The Congress panel comprises party UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, state president Aradhana Mishra (Mona), state working president Imran Masood, and AICC general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal.The structured panels mark a formal start to opposition coordination within the INDIA bloc ahead of the crucial 2027 polls. The Congress had earlier indicated interest in contesting a large number of seats (reports had mentioned a list of around 181 constituencies), while the SP has consistently maintained that the formula must rest on local strength, past performance, and realistic winning prospects. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the SP had won 111 seats while the Congress secured only two.Leaders indicated that the two-day first phase (November 23–24) would examine seats constituency by constituency, with a focus on avoiding vote division against the BJP and ensuring the alliance maximises its overall tally. Both sides expressed confidence that the process would be wrapped up quickly, with further meetings scheduled if needed.

headline: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar invites Toyota to expand manufacturing operations, eyes 1 million vehicle capacity
content: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday assured Toyota Motor Corporation of his government's full support and facilitation for expanding its manufacturing operations in Karnataka, as the Japanese automobile major looks at scaling its vehicle production capacity to one million in the near future.During a meeting with the senior leadership of Toyota Motor Corporation at its Motomachi plant in Japan, the CM, along with Minister for Large and Medium Industries M B Patil, discussed opportunities to strengthen Toyota's manufacturing footprint, expand production and explore new mobility solutions in Karnataka, officials said.Also Read: Toyota to open third plant in Karnataka, aims to produce 1 lakh units annuallyThe Toyota delegation was led by Masakazu Yoshimura, Chairman, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Toyota Motor Corporation, they said.According to a statement issued by the Chief Minister's office, the company highlighted Karnataka's importance as a key manufacturing destination and export hub, besides outlining its existing presence and operations in the State.The chief minister assured the Toyota leadership that the Karnataka government would extend all necessary support to facilitate the company's expansion plans.He encouraged Toyota to further scale up its operations in the state, reiterating Karnataka's commitment to providing a conducive environment for investments and manufacturing growth.Also Read: Karnataka CM urges Czech firms to invest beyond Bengaluru, explore energy, aerospace sectorsDuring the discussions, Shivakumar also encouraged Toyota to consider introducing its Japan taxi model in Karnataka. The affordable hybrid electric vehicle, designed for taxi operations, could help make taxi services more economical and accessible to commuters across the state, it said.The meeting also deliberated on the possibility of rolling out flex-fuel vehicles and their potential advantages, particularly in the context of alternative fuels and sustainable mobility solutions, it said.The chief minister and Patil invited the Toyota leadership to participate in the upcoming Global Investors Meet and explore further investment opportunities in Karnataka, officials said.Following the meeting, Shivakumar and the Industries Minister visited Toyota's Motomachi plant, the company's first flagship passenger car manufacturing facility in Asia, established in 1959, they said.The facility currently assembles multiple vehicle models powered by different technologies, including hybrid electric vehicles, battery electric vehicles and fuel cell electric vehicles, it said.The delegation was briefed on the plant's manufacturing capabilities, production processes and technological advancements in automobile manufacturing.An important highlight of the visit was the interaction with more than 20 members of Toyota's Global Skill-up training programme from Karnataka. The trainees, who are graduates of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the State, are currently undergoing specialised training in Japan, officials said.The CM and the Industries minister interacted with the trainees, enquired about their training experience and encouraged them to make the best use of the international exposure and technical expertise they were gaining.The trainees expressed their gratitude to the chief minister and the minister for taking time out to meet them during their visit to Japan, it said.The delegation also visited the Toyota Kaikan Museum, which showcases the company's manufacturing philosophy, technological innovations and vision for the future of mobility, officials said.The visit is part of Karnataka's ongoing international investment outreach aimed at strengthening industrial partnerships, attracting fresh investments, expanding manufacturing capabilities and creating skilled employment opportunities in the state, they added.Also Read: Toyota halts output at Karnataka facilityEarlier in the day, Shivakumar along with Patil, also travelled by the Shinkansen bullet train from Tokyo to Nagoya as part of their Japan visit, ahead of their engagement with Toyota.Posting a video of their travel on social media platform 'X', the chief minister said Japan's high-speed rail is a remarkable example of how innovation, technology and infrastructure can transform the way people live, work and travel."Travelled by the Shinkansen bullet train from Tokyo to Nagoya as part of our Japan visit, ahead of our engagement with Toyota, along with M B Patil, Minister for Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development," he said.He asserted that the state government's focus is to strengthen industrial partnerships, attract investments and create new opportunities for Karnataka."By learning from global best practices and fostering meaningful collaborations, we aim to advance Karnataka's growth through innovation, infrastructure and sustainable development," he added.

headline: PM Modi gifts Gangajal to Nepal's Balen Shah; receives Rudraksh, Chandan from Pashupatinath in return
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday gifted his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah a kalash of Gangajal from Triveni. Shah is on a two-day state visit to India from November 22 to 23, his first visit to the country since assuming office in March 2026.While Shah presented Modi with Rudraksh and Chandan from the sacred Pashupatinath Temple, news agency ANI reported.Shah also held bilateral talks with Modi at Hyderabad House on Monday, followed by a call on President Droupadi Murmu. According to the ministry of external affairs (MEA), the discussions would cover the entire spectrum of bilateral relations and regional and international developments of mutual interest. Track Nepal PM India visit LIVE updates here."Prime Minister Modi will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister of Nepal on 23 November 2026 to review the full range of India–Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest," the ministry stated.The MEA also highlighted the historical, cultural and civilisational foundations of India-Nepal relations, noting that cooperation between the two countries has expanded across traditional as well as emerging sectors."India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports," the ministry said.PM Modi to host luncheonModi will also host an official luncheon in honour of Shah and his 34-member government delegation.The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit. The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives.Earlier today, Shah paid floral tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat and wrote in the memorial's visitor book, describing truth as "a power unmatched by any force" and compassion as "the ultimate strength"."At this sacred place, I pay profound homage to Mahatma Gandhi, whose life proved to the world that truth possesses a power unmatched by any force," Shah wrote in his signed message.Linking Gandhi's legacy with Nepal's heritage, the Nepalese prime minister added, “On behalf of the people and Government of Nepal, I offer my deepest tribute. Coming from the birthplace of Lord Buddha, I behold in Gandhiji's legacy that very same immortal light: the profound truth that compassion is the ultimate strength, and that true leadership lies in selfless service to the humblest among us.”Reaffirming Kathmandu's commitment to bilateral ties, he wrote, “In honouring Gandhiji's timeless spirit, I reaffirm Nepal's solemn commitment to nurture this enduring bond with deep honesty, mutual respect, and unwavering trust.”The Raj Ghat visit came after Shah was accorded a ceremonial guard of honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan earlier on Monday, with Modi in attendance.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: Chief Minister Vijay to meet legislators of TVK-led ruling alliance in Chennai today
content: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay is scheduled to meet legislators of Tamil Nadu’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led ruling alliance in Chennai on Monday afternoon, people aware of the matter said. The people added that the meeting is scheduled at 3pm at Bamani Illam, the chief minister’s official residence.The meeting is being held a day after the Tamil Nadu government moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its November 20 order allowing the “Karthigai Deepam” to be lit as a one-time measure at the disputed stone pillar, or the deepathoon, atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.The court has been hearing appeals against a Madras high court orders permitting the lighting of the lamp near the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah.The dispute concerns Hindu devotees’ demands to light the Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar approximately 50 metres from a dargah. The Opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) accused the state government of failing to properly argue the Deepathoon case in the Supreme Court and botching it. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said Lord Murugan devotees will teach the government a lesson over its stand on matter.Vijay’s meeting with the lawmakers of the ruling alliance is being held days after he met his party legislators at a resort in Mahabalipuram on November 11 against the backdrop of controversies.Assembly deputy speaker M Ravi Shankar drew flak after a video surfaced on social media purportedly showing him allegedly assaulting a person who approached him to submit a petition regarding civic issues in his locality in Thuraiyur. TVK lawmaker C Arul Vignesh faced allegations of sending obscene messages to a district collector even as he denied the charges, terming them “baseless.”On November 12, TVK deputy general secretary CTR Nirmal Kumar said the meeting with party lawmakers was a regular one, and the party high command gave instructions to the lawmakers. He refused to go into specifics.The TVK formed a post-poll alliance with the Congress, Indian Union Muslim League, and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi. The Communist Party of India and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) extended outside support. The TVK-led government completed six months in office after assuming power in May 2026.

headline: CJI Surya Kant recuses from Supertech insolvency case, says applicant ‘remotely known’ to him
content: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday recused himself from hearing a case related to the monitoring of Supertech projects undergoing insolvency proceedings, citing his acquaintance with one of the applicants.A bench headed by the CJI said, “I am recusing from this matter. One applicant is known to me. Not that he is my relative... But someone remotely known to me.”The matter relates to the insolvency proceedings involving 16 distressed projects of Supertech, which are being executed by the government’s construction arm, NBCC India Limited. The projects comprise nearly 50,000 dwelling units across Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Karnataka, and are pending before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).The CJI, who was heading a bench also comprising justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, released the matter and said, “I will have to constitute a special bench. This applicant is incidentally known to me. Somebody should have been conscious of this fact. Why unnecessarily become a party?”The court had last heard the matter on October 27, when it took up an application filed by amicus curiae and advocate Rajiv Jain, who sought the appointment of a court-monitored committee to oversee the completion of the 16 projects.On the previous occasion, the court had criticised the slow progress made by NBCC, observing, “We have realised nothing is happening. Either we dissolve the committee and appoint a receiver as we did in the Amrapali matters or like the Unitech matter, where the government constituted a board of directors in public interest to construct the stalled projects.”NBCC has also faced criticism from homebuyers, who pointed out that more than ₹30 crore had been spent on hiring the company since it was appointed project management consultant (PMC) for the 16 Supertech projects by the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) in December 2024, without a single tender being issued.At present, an Apex Court Committee (ACC) is overseeing the construction of the 16 Supertech projects. The committee is headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice (retd) Krishna Murari and includes representatives of financial institutions, NBCC and real estate experts.The Supreme Court is separately hearing a petition filed by NBCC seeking exemptions under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) to complete the insolvency-hit Supertech projects. In May, the NCLAT had refused to grant the exemption and rejected NBCC’s plea for enhanced fees on the sale of unfinished flats in the 16 projects.The court had also listed the matter for hearing all stakeholders on the way forward, including the possibility of disbanding the ACC and allowing the construction work to be carried out under an independent court-appointed receiver.It had said that homebuyers would not be burdened further, pointing to unsold inventory and vacant plots within the projects as potential sources of funds to complete the stalled construction work.

headline: DMK, BJP criticise Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay over Thirupparankundram lamp-lighting row | India News
content: The Opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) has accused Tamil Nadu’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)-led government of failing to properly argue the Deepathoon case in the Supreme Court and botching it, even as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said Lord Murugan devotees will teach it a lesson over its stand on matter.BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran questioned why Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay was agitated over the lighting at the temple and the first abode of Lord Murugan. He slammed the Tamil Nadu government for moving the Supreme Court to review its November 20 order allowing the Karthigai Deepam to be lit as a one-time measure at the disputed stone pillar (Deepathoon) atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.“Should Joseph Vijay stoop this low for the sake of vote bank politics?” he asked in a social media post on Monday. He added that Lord Murugan’s devotees would teach a lesson to the anti-Hindu government, which systematically snatches their worship rights while claiming to govern for all.On Saturday, the state government filed the review petition, a day after the Supreme Court’s interim order allowing the lamp lighting on Tuesday.DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin said the ruling party and the Chief Minister must answer for the failure to properly argue the case. “It has been two days since our leader [MK Stalin] spoke about this, and the chief minister has not opened his mouth,” he said.He said MK Stalin declared that they will face the consequences on the Thirupparankundram issue during their rule. “Thalaivar [MK Stalin] not only said that, but he protected religious harmony and social justice under the DMK rule.” He said their leader foiled the BJP’s plans to incite riots.Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam chief Vaiko, whose party is an ally of the ruling TVK-led Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance, said the Supreme Court judgement saddened them. “For hundreds of years, the practice was that they would light the lamp near the Mandapam. Never did they go to the top and light the lamp on that pillar. This will hurt the sentiments of the people living together in harmony, Muslims and Hindus....Thirupparankundram is a historic place, and this is an unwarranted thing.” The Supreme Court has been hearing appeals against a Madras high court orders permitting the lighting of the lamp near the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Dargah.The dispute concerns Hindu devotees’ demands to light the Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar approximately 50 metres from a dargah.

headline: 'Two GTA-Gyanesh Theft Arrangers' stars exposed: Congress dig at PM Modi-Amit Shah jodi
content: <p>New Delhi: The Congress on Monday claimed that the continued suspense over the Parliament session is suggestive of either the "<a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/gta-vi-buzz-bjp-hits-back-with-upa-era-2004-2014-video-after-congress-jibes-at-pm-post-4224926">PM-HM jodi</a>" being trapped by its own bluff and bluster or there is something "truly sinister" that is being planned.</p>.<p>The opposition party said either way the "two <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/from-dhruva-to-rockstar-how-bengaluru-helped-shape-gta-and-red-dead-4223398">GTA </a>(Gyanesh Theft Arrangers)" stars stand brutally exposed but sadly, the institution of Parliament is being further diminished greatly by the shenanigans of the "diabolical duo".</p>.<p>Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh asked what games are being played by Prime Minister Narendra Modi-Home Minister Amit Shah "jodi, assuming that the jodi is still together".</p>.<p>"By now, the nation should have known when the Winter Session of Parliament will take place, assuming that there is to be a Winter Session. By now the nation should have known when the Monsoon Session that has yet to be prorogued will be reconvened, assuming it is to be reconvened," Ramesh said on X.</p>.PM Modi uses GTA VI release meme to highlight India's progress; apt as the game follows a 'criminal duo,' mocks Congress.<p>By now, having seen through their desperate efforts of the 'jodi' to cobble together a "super-tainted two-thirds majority" in the Lok Sabha, the nation is entitled to know what the PM-HM formula for delimitation is, assuming that there is indeed one, he said.</p>.<p>"The continued suspense clearly is suggestive of two things: (i) the jodi is confused and is trapped by its own bluff and bluster; or (ii) there is something truly sinister that is being planned," Ramesh said.</p>.<p>"Either way, the two GTA (Gyanesh Theft Arrangers) stars stand brutally exposed. Sadly, the institution of Parliament, already badly bruised, is being further diminished greatly by the shenanigans of the diabolical duo," he said in a wordplay on the recently-launched video game GTA-VI (Grand Theft Auto).</p>.<p>The Congress on Saturday said that 100 days have passed since the Monsoon session of Parliament was adjourned sine die, but Prime Minister Modi and Union Home Minister Shah are still in search of a "supertainted" two-thirds majority in Lok Sabha to get the delimitation bill passed.</p>.<p>Ramesh had said it is in the nation's interest to let the current Lok Sabha strength and state-wise configuration continue with one-third reservation for women implemented till the Viksit Bharat objective is achieved.</p>

headline: Proposal to rename West Bengal as 'Paschim Banga' to be tabled in next assembly session: CM
content: <p>Kolkata: A proposal to rename <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/india/west-bengal">West Bengal</a> as 'Paschim Banga' will be tabled in the assembly during the next session, beginning on December 4, <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/suvendu-adhikari">Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari</a> said on Monday.</p>.<p>The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Adhikari.</p>.<p>"The proposal to rename West Bengal as 'Paschim Banga' will be tabled in the House on December 9," he said after the meeting.</p>.Calcutta High Court extends interim protection to TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee till February 26 in six criminal cases.<p>Once the proposal is passed by the assembly, it will be sent to the Centre for its approval, he said.</p>.<p>The winter session of the assembly will be held from December 4 to 14. </p>

headline: CM Revanth puts Congress dissidents on notice
content: HYDERABAD: Amid growing dissidence within the ruling Telangana Congress, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday cautioned party leaders that their conduct and speeches were being closely monitored.“We will assess everyone’s contribution at the time of elections. We recognise those who work hard. We also remember those who work hard to undermine the party. We will certainly remember them. If you remain within the party line, positions will come to your doorstep automatically,” Revanth said.Addressing an extensive meeting of the Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC), Revanth said the party had given positions to 65 people who had worked in various affiliated wings.“It is a misconception that positions can be secured merely by making rounds of Gandhi Bhavan or Delhi. You need not go to Delhi. You must go to villages, tribal hamlets and the homes of the poor. Only those who stand by the poor and become their trusted companions can emerge as Congress leaders. Positions are earned through commitment to the party and hard work,” he said..Carry Cong flag with pride, make Rahul PM: RevanthRevanth said the party had complete information about what leaders said in public and what they discussed behind closed doors. He, however, said that a performance assessment would be carried out once every five years.The chief minister expressed confidence that the Congress would retain power after the 2029 Assembly elections by securing one crore votes and winning around 90 Assembly seats. He also listed the schemes launched by the Congress government in the state over the last three years.On nominated posts, he said leaders who were currently disappointed would receive recognition in the future.Stating that Telangana had always stood by the Congress during difficult times, Revanth called upon party workers to stand firmly behind Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi as well.“Let us carry the Congress flag with pride and work together to make Rahul the prime minister,” he told party leaders..Earlier, at the PCC Political Affairs Committee (PAC) meeting, four resolutions were adopted, including one welcoming newly appointed AICC Telangana in-charge BM Sandeep and another thanking outgoing in-charge Meenakshi Natarajan.The PAC decided to write to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre to provide financial assistance of Rs 30,000 crore to Telangana to mitigate the impact of drought and declare it a national disaster.The PAC also called for a separate column for OBC caste enumeration in the 2027 Census to ensure an accurate count of Other Backward Classes (OBCs).Meanwhile, belligerent Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy once again took to social media on Sunday, making it clear that he was not prepared to step back. “My journey will not stop. My struggle will not end. I will never take a step back when it comes to fighting for the people!” he posted..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: BRS gave AP free rein over water projects: CM Revanth Reddy
content: HYDERABAD: Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy on Sunday alleged that Andhra Pradesh had initiated the Palnadu Water Grid scheme in 2022, during the tenures of K Chandrasekhar Rao and YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, stating that a government order sanctioning Rs 1,580 crore under the Union government’s Jal Jeevan Mission had been issued that year.Addressing the Congress Political Affairs Committee (PAC) and Advisory Committee meeting at Gandhi Bhavan, Revanth claimed that the Pothireddypadu project was initiated when the BRS was in power and that the AP government had taken up projects during the same period. “Andhra Pradesh has not taken up a single project since the Congress came to power in Telangana,” he said, referring to water-sharing disputes with the neighbouring state.He alleged that former chief minister K Chandrasekhar Rao had signed an agreement for 299 tmcft of water, on the basis of which AP had undertaken projects. He also claimed that the previous BRS government had not sanctioned funds even for land acquisition for these projects.Push for caste censusRevanth said Telangana had conducted a caste census for the first time in 100 years and urged the Centre to undertake a similar exercise with a column for OBCs alongside the Census 2027. He suggested that the PAC adopt a resolution seeking a caste census and that TPCC president Mahesh Kumar Goud write to the prime minister on the issue.Welcoming new AICC Telangana in-charge BM Sandeep Kumar, Revanth thanked Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, party president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi for appointing him. .El Nino: Revanth seeks Centre’s aidExpressing concern over El Nino and its impact on agriculture, Revanth said inadequate rainfall was affecting crop prospects and urged farmers to opt for crops that require less water. He said the state had adequate foodgrain stocks and had managed to supply power to farmers even when demand touched 20,000 MW during the monsoon, helping protect standing crops.He said nearly 100 countries were facing El Nino-related difficulties, while neighbouring Maharashtra and Karnataka were also experiencing drought-like conditions. Telangana would have to ensure drinking water supply for the next eight months, and water stored in irrigation projects might have to be diverted for drinking purposes, the chief minister added.Estimating that Rs 30,000 crore would be needed to tackle the situation, Revanth sought financial assistance from the Centre and urged the PAC to adopt resolutions demanding support.‘SIR could lead to large-scale voter deletions’The chief minister expressed concern over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that it could lead to large-scale deletion of voters. Citing electoral data, he said India had 91 crore voters against a population of 130 crore in 2019, while the voter count stood at 97.5 crore against a population of 140 crore in 2024..He alleged that around 13 crore names had already been deleted and claimed the exercise could result in up to 20 crore voters being removed. Dalits, Adivasis and women were particularly vulnerable to exclusion, he said, adding that migration was among the reasons cited for deleting names.Accusing the BJP-led Union government of using SIR to remove voters instead of ensuring the inclusion of all eligible citizens, Revanth claimed that 71 lakh voters had been kept aside in Telangana. He urged Congress Booth Level Officers to remain vigilant, alleging that names were being deleted mechanically, even when surnames did not match correctly.He called on party leaders to monitor electoral rolls continuously instead of waiting until elections, and alleged that the BJP was creating two categories of citizens, those with voting rights and those without, potentially reducing sections of the population to second-class citizens.‘Praja Balam’ outreach from SankrantiRevanth also announced a five-month public outreach programme, Praja Balam, beginning with Sankranti to strengthen the party’s connect with people.Revanth tells leaders to focus on villages, jobsRevanth urged leaders to visit every village and ensure people had access to employment opportunities, assuring them that funds would not be a constraint. He further addressed concerns over public statements by party MLAs and reiterated the Congress’s commitment to returning to power. The chief minister said he would fully follow the party high command’s directions, asserting that retaining power was essential to ensuring the welfare of party workers.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Probe Naveen Patnaik’s trips and yours too: BJD to CM Majhi
content: BHUBANESWAR: The BJD on Sunday doubled down on its attack on Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi over the inquiry into the foreign visits of former chief minister Naveen Patnaik, retired IAS officer VK Pandian and IPS officer Ravi Kant, demanding that the probe also cover overseas trips undertaken by the present CM, his deputies and senior government officials.Addressing a media-conference here, senior party spokesperson Lenin Mohanty and MLA Goutam Buddha Das said the BJD welcomed the investigation but the chief minister must also be transparent about his own foreign visits as well as those of his ministers and officials.The BJD leaders alleged that Majhi had deliberately raised an irrelevant issue to divert public attention from the government’s mismanagement of Ganjam floods, which caused large-scale devastation in the district.They also raised the seven-day visit of deputy chief minister Pravati Parida to London from November 2 to 9 in 2024, to promote tourism and attract investment. Demanding that the government disclose what tangible benefits Odisha’s tourism sector had derived from the trip, they alleged that her entourage included a large number of non-official members.“The deputy chief minister is now on a visit to Indonesia and Bali with a large entourage while the winter session of the Assembly is on. The BJD will raise this in the House, along with the foreign visits of other ministers and officials,” they said..The BJD leaders also questioned the role of Industries secretary Hemant Sharma, who holds additional charge of the Home department, in the probe into the former CM’s foreign trips.Pointing to earlier inquiries, they said the government had launched investigation into three issues against the previous regime and its former minister but failed to establish any wrongdoing.“Before the 2024 elections, several top BJP leaders had visited Odisha and spread propaganda that the Ratna Bhandar of Lord Jagannath had been looted and the valuables taken to Tamil Nadu. After coming to power, the BJP government ordered an inquiry and eventually gave a clean chit,” they said.False claims were also made about then 5T secretary VK Pandian’s helicopter trips. The state government’s allegations were proven baseless, with the Khurda District and Sessions Court subsequently giving him a clean chit, they stated.On the missing inquiry report file relating to the assassination of Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati in Kandhamal, the BJD leaders alleged that the BJP government tried to shift the blame from itself by dragging Pandian into the controversy..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: CM Majhi Hears 15,667 Grievances in 20 Sessions, Disposes of 96% Cases
content: Bhubaneswar: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has conducted 20 public grievance hearing sessions since assuming office in June 2024, during which 15,667 grievances were received and 14,983 cases, or nearly 96 per cent, have been disposed of. This was informed by parliamentary affairs minister Dr Mukesh Mahaling in the State Assembly on Monday while replying to a question raised by Biju Janata Dal (BJD) MLA Sarada Prasanna Jena of Balikuda-Erasama. Mahaling said the BJP government had revived the public grievance hearing mechanism, which, according to him, had been discontinued by the previous BJD government. A dedicated online portal was also introduced to facilitate registration of public complaints. ”The previous government had stopped listening to the grievances of the people. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi restarted the grievance hearing mechanism and a dedicated portal was opened for registration of complaints. So far, we have disposed of 96 per cent of the cases. The remaining grievances are being actively examined and will be resolved on their merits,” Mahaling told the House. Responding to concerns raised by Jena and senior BJD member Pramila Mallick over the functioning of the grievance redressal mechanism, the minister said the government was considering further improvements to the portal through technological upgradation. Mahaling also assured the Assembly that technical glitches reported in the online grievance registration system would be addressed. The exchange took a political turn when the minister questioned the BJD's criticism of the present government's grievance redressal mechanism. Defending Majhi's approach, he challenged Jena to state how many times former Chief Minister and Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik had personally heard public grievances during his tenure. “Our government is quite sensitive to listening to the grievances of the people. Will the BJD member say how many times his leader Naveen Patnaik personally heard public grievances, as the present Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi does?” Mahaling asked. Naveen Patnaik, who was present in the Assembly when Mahaling made the remarks, is the Leader of the Opposition. Separately, replying to a query from BJD MLA Arvind Mohapatra regarding technical problems in the grievance registration portal, Mahaling reiterated that the government would take steps to resolve the glitches. The government maintained that it was committed to strengthening the grievance redressal system and ensuring that public complaints were addressed in a time-bound manner.

headline: RBI plans to tap broker apps to boost retail trading in government bonds
content: India's central bank plans to allow online brokerages to offer retail investors access to trade government securities next year, ​two people familiar with the matter said.The Reserve Bank of ​India's move is designed to broaden the investor base for the $2.3 trillion sovereign debt ‌market, which remains largely institutional. Government securities are a relatively low-risk option compared with equities and other instruments, and they offer a hedge against stock market volatility.The central bank's own RBI Retail Direct platform, launched in 2021 to attract retail traders, has so far drawn a muted response.Allowing private online trading platforms to connect directly to the portal would allow access to the growing retail base, said one industry executive who is familiar with the conversations.A committee of top online brokers is being formed to facilitate this technical integration, the two people added.Brokerages are expected to link with the RBI's ‌system via an application programming interface, the second person said.Both officials requested anonymity because the discussions are confidential. The RBI did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.TAPPING RETAIL MOMENTUMIndian online brokerages have been key to a boom in retail investor numbers since the COVID pandemic.Over 130 million retail investors now trade equities directly, up from around 27 million in 2019, according to NSE data.Their participation helped Indian stock markets rally to record highs. ​However, the stock market's underperformance over the last two years has prompted retail investors to look for better ‌opportunities elsewhere, including corporate debt.The RBI Retail Direct platform showed about 403,000 participants in mid-November, higher than the 67,000 in December 2022, with total holdings at ₹4,885 crore ($527.14 ‌million).The portal offers individual investors the opportunity to trade government securities, treasury bills, state development loans, and ‌sovereign gold bonds in both primary auctions and the secondary market.Top online brokerage Groww has around 13.7 million active investors investing through its platform, while Angel One and Zerodha ‌have ​around 7 million ​each.Market participants said seamless integration and faster settlements will be critical to attract retail users accustomed to managing stocks, mutual funds and corporate debt under a ‌single brokerage application.

headline: UK Minister to Tell Business Public Control Is in Its Interest
content: (Bloomberg) -- The British government will seek to persuade business leaders to support greater public control of water and energy utilities, arguing that the approach would improve services and lower costs without requiring wholesale nationalization.Louise Haigh, Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s First Secretary of State, will deliver the message at the annual conference of the CBI, a leading UK business lobbying group, on Monday.“Public control is not anti-business - it’s about getting the foundations right, so that private enterprise can do what it does best,” Haigh will say, according to excerpts of her speech released ahead of time by the Cabinet Office.Haigh is expected to argue that the current system has left businesses facing high energy prices, delays in connecting to the electricity grid and unreliable services that hinder economic growth. She will also contend that leaving essential services such as water and energy largely to the market has created effective monopolies with little genuine competition.Her speech is also intended to reassure businesses that greater public control doesn’t necessarily mean wholesale nationalization. Before taking office in July, Burnham promised to bring the water industry into public ownership but has since focused on expanding government control of utilities.Haigh will also use the speech to criticize previous generations of politicians for “ducking difficult decisions” and “outsourcing responsibility to a sprawling web of regulators and arms-length bodies.”She is also expected to outline plans for greater government support to help British companies invest and grow, along with a new partnership with private investors based on clear rules and expectations and a fair return on investment.Political rivals, meanwhile, will use their appearances before business leaders to criticize Burnham’s efforts to forge closer ties with the European Union.Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch will argue that the 0.4% boost to gross domestic product promised by Burnham’s new trade agreement with the EU isn’t enough to justify closer alignment with European rules, according to excerpts of her speech released ahead of the conference.“The question has always been: is it worth locking yourself into one market if it locks you out of another?” Badenoch will say. “You have to weigh the benefits up against the cost. Of course, Europe will always remain an important market, but it is not the market of the future.”Reform UK leader Nigel Farage will focus on the prospect of reversing Brexit. Farage will argue that closer ties with the EU would benefit big businesses at the expense of smaller firms, which have fewer resources to deal with additional regulations, according to an advance copy of his remarks.Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said Sunday on the BBC that “all the options will be on the table,” including potentially rejoining the bloc, in Burnham’s upcoming talks with Brussels.More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: DA hike: Tripura increases dearness allowance by 3% to 44% of basic salary; CM says component enhanced by 36% since 2022
content: DA hike: Tripura enhanced dearness allowance and dearness relief (DR) for state government employees and pensioners by 3% in October, to 44% of basic salary — an increase of 8% this year and 36% since 2022, according to Chief Minister Manik Saha.The Tripura Cabinet announced a second hike in DA and DR, and increased the House Rent Allowance (HRA) for government employees to 10% of basic pay, subject to a ceiling of ₹10,000 per month, with effect from 1 October 2026, according to a report by India Today.The hike will put an additional annual burden of about ₹300 crore on the state exchequer, Saha added.Tripura govt declares 5% DA hikeNotably, this came after the state declared a 5% DA and DR increase for government employees, effective from 1 April, at an additional ₹500 crore annually, Saha said. He also added that 1,02,563 state government employees and 81,019 pensioners will benefit from the increase.“We are continuously trying to increase the DA for the employees to narrow the gap with their central government counterparts,” he stated, as per a PTI report. This is in reference to the Centre providing 60% DA to central government employees as of last month and 58% prior to that.Tripura has raised DA by 36% since 2022: CMAddressing a BJP programme in Agartala on Sunday, 22 November, ahead of the civic polls scheduled for Friday, 27 November, Saha stated that his government has increased DA by 36 percentage points since July 2022 — from 8% to 44% to narrow the gap between state and central government counterparts, PTI reported.“No government in the Northeast has increased DA by 36% in such a short period. It shows the present government's efforts to reduce the gap between state employees and central government staff. If we don't reduce the DA gap, the state as a whole will be a loser, since it receives funds to pay its employees and pensioners. A total of ₹100 crore is needed to release 1% DA/ DR,” he said.Regarding the revision of their pay during the tenure of the 8th Pay Commission, he said the state is committed. “I have discussed the pay revision issue with Finance Minister Pranajit Singha Roy. The Centre has already made progress towards implementing revised pay structures. We will definitely do it,” Saha added.He further added that the previous government had implemented a 2.25 fitment factor under the 7th Pay Commission, while the BJP-led leadership raised it to 2.57 in July 2018, resulting in an average salary increase of 8% for employees.He also stressed maintaining pay parity with central government employees and said the state is investing heavily in capital expenditure to sustain economic growth.(With inputs from PTI)

headline: PM Modi and Nepal’s Balendra Shah Hold Key Talks at Hyderabad House
content: New Delhi, Nov 23: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, on Monday met at Hyderabad House, discussing ways to strengthen cooperation across several sectors.During the bilateral discussions, the two leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.Additionally, both leaders will virtually flag off the Saryu-Kamala Express from New Delhi.Following the bilateral talks, the two leaders will jointly address a press conference. Prime Minister Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of the Nepali Prime Minister and his delegation on the same day.Earlier in the day, Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan on Monday. Prime Minister Modi warmly welcomed Shah upon his arrival at the Rashtrapati Bhavan.Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day State visit to India at the invitation of Prime Minister Modi. Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Jitin Prasada welcomed him at the airport.Shah will additionally call on President Droupadi Murmu during his visit.The Nepali Prime Minister is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials, forming a 35-member government delegation.A separate 52-member delegation comprising business representatives will also participate in the visit at their own expense.The bilateral discussions are expected to cover post-flood reconstruction assistance, energy, trade, connectivity and broader cooperation between the two neighbouring countries.The two sides are also expected to unveil a Joint Vision Document titled "Samriddha Nepal, Samunnat Bharat" (Prosperous Nepal, Developed India), which will set long-term bilateral goals and concrete targets for cooperation.During the visit, the two countries are also expected to inaugurate several completed projects related to connectivity and energy cooperation and lay the foundation stones for new projects.According to Nepal's Foreign Ministry, discussions will focus on strengthening economic cooperation in areas including trade, transportation, investment, energy, connectivity networks and infrastructure development.The two sides will also exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering cooperation in education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.(IANS)
