headline: Masjid Qalandari, Shahi Maqbara, mazars, homes razed in Ujjain as Congress MP slams BJP's "bulldozer politics" ahead of Simhastha 2028
content:
Congress MP Syed Naseer Hussain has accused the BJP of "bulldozer politics" as mosques, mazars, graves and Muslim homes are demolished in Ujjain ahead of Simhastha 2028.

Congress Rajya Sabha MP Syed Naseer Hussain has questioned the demolition of Muslim religious structures, graves and homes in Ujjain as part of the preparations for the Simhastha Kumbh in 2028, alleging that the action is disproportionately hitting Muslim communities.

In a post on X on Sunday, Hussain said several structures near Madhav Nagar Railway Station had been demolished, including mazars, Masjid Qalandari, the Shahi Maqbara and houses belonging to the mutawalli.

He also claimed that around 80 religious structures across Ujjain had already been removed or relocated as part of development projects ahead of the religious congregation.

"Why must Muslim places of worship, graves and homes be bulldozed in the name of Simhastha-2028?" Hussain asked. He accused the BJP of pursuing "bulldozer politics" that threatens the heritage, dignity and sense of security of minority communities.

Questioning the legal basis of the demolitions, the Congress leader asked whether due process was being followed, and described the action as part of what he called a politics of intimidation.

Simhastha 2028 is a massive Hindu pilgrimage and sacred festival, scheduled to be held in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, from March 27 to May 27, 2028. Held once every 12 years, the event is expected to draw millions of devotees. The Madhya Pradesh government and the local administration have taken up infrastructure, sanitation and urban development projects across the city ahead of the festival.

Earlier, the Madhya Pradesh High Court dismissed two petitions challenging notices issued by the Ujjain Municipal Corporation seeking the removal of portions of the historic Shahi Masjid for road widening ahead of Simhastha 2028.

headline: "Don't need advice from you": Congress' Gurjeet Singh Aujla hits back at Nitin Nabin; challenges PM to live debate
content: Amritsar (Punjab) [India], November 23 (ANI): Congress MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla on Monday hit back at Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national president Nitin Nabin over his remarks against Rahul Gandhi, saying the Congress did not need any advice from him.He also challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to participate in a live debate and respond to the issues raised by the Congress leader.Speaking to ANI in Amritsar, Aujla said the Congress, being an old political party, was well aware of what was good for the country and did not require advice from the BJP."I would like to tell Nitin Nabin that the Congress party is twice as old as you are. The Congress party itself knows very well what is good for the country and what is not; we do not need any advice from you. Rahul Gandhi is a popular leader across the entire nation. He focuses his politics on substantive issues," Aujla said.He further alleged that the BJP was avoiding answering the issues raised by Rahul Gandhi and instead resorting to remarks against him."You have no answers—that is why you resort to such talk. Instead, provide responses to the issues raised by Rahul Gandhi. Do so in Parliament, or challenge your Prime Minister to a live debate—ask him to participate and provide answers there," he added.Meanwhile, Congress General Secretary and Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot on Monday criticised the reported possibility of a renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) in Punjab, calling it "pure opportunism" and questioning what had changed since the two parties parted ways.Pilot also raised concerns over the voter list and the voting process, saying several complaints had emerged since Gyanesh Kumar became the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC), warranting an impartial investigation."Ever since Gyanesh Kumar became a CEC, numerous complaints have emerged regarding the voter list and the voting process itself, which necessitate an impartial investigation. We have filed a petition in the Supreme Court, and the court will now deliver its verdict. The disagreements expressed by the other Election Commissioners concerning the voter list and 'Form 6' are significant issues. The Election Commission, not the government, must provide a clarification on these matters," he said.Commenting on the political developments since the 2024 elections, Pilot said the Congress and the INDIA alliance had performed remarkably well, while claiming that the present NDA government lacked an absolute majority and depended on two allies."People across the country have realised that the BJP's downfall is inevitable. This is why they are breaking apart various political parties," he said.Referring to the political developments in Punjab, Pilot said seven AAP MPs had moved to the NDA and two AAP MLAs had joined the BJP, questioning how the public could trust a party whose own elected representatives were leaving it."If the AAP's own MPs and MLAs lack faith in their own party, how can the public be expected to trust it?" he asked.Pilot further claimed that the BJP's standing was set to decline nationwide and cited the recent Panchayat elections in Rajasthan, saying the electorate had voted overwhelmingly in favour of the Congress. He also questioned the BJP's reported efforts to reconnect with the Akali Dal, asking what compulsion had prompted the move. He reiterated that the Congress was aiming for a clear majority to form the government in Punjab.Further, Punjab Congress Vice President Dr Raj Kumar Verka said Pilot's visit to different streets and villages across the state was aimed at understanding the difficulties faced by party workers and the public.Verka said Pilot was examining local issues and gathering information about concerns such as the drug situation, corruption and law and order in Punjab."People are talking about how the drug situation in Punjab has gone from bad to worse; they are discussing corruption and the state of law and order. Sachin Pilot is also gathering information from those who have been forced to pay extortion money, or who have received threatening letters or phone calls," Verka said.He added that the Congress would incorporate these concerns into its election manifesto, which would reflect the hardships and sentiments of the people. "I believe it will be (announced) by December," Verka said.The remarks come ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, with political parties gearing up for the electoral contest in the state. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has declared 71 candidates for the 117-member Punjab Legislative Assembly. (ANI)

headline: Despire Court Orders to File FIR Against Tripura Minister Over Alleged Fake Certificate, Police Say Order Yet to Arrive
content: Agartala: Five days after a judicial magistrate in Tripura’s Unakoti district ordered police to register an FIR against state cabinet minister and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Tinku Roy over allegedly forged Class 12 certificates, the officer-in-charge of Kailashahar police station said they have still not received the order.Speaking to The Wire on Saturday (November 21), officer-in-charge Tapash Malakar confirmed that no official copy of the November 16 directive had reached the station. The court has directed the police to expedite the investigation and submit a report by December 17.The order by Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Ranjabati Roy came after nearly 11 months in which no FIR was registered on a complaint against Roy, whose cabinet portfolios include Social Welfare and Social Education. While rejecting months of police opposition in court and directing an FIR, the magistrate clarified that she was expressing no opinion on whether the allegations against Roy are true.The Wire tried to contact minister Roy over the phone on Saturday, November 21, at 9:47 AM for his response to the court order and the allegations, but he did not answer the call.A Class 12 certificate from a board flagged as fakeAt the centre of the controversy is an educational qualification that Roy declared in both his 2018 and 2023 election affidavits. In his nomination papers from the Chandipur assembly constituency in 2023, as well as from Kurti-Kadamtala in 2018, Roy stated that he passed Class 12 in 2004 from the “Board of Secondary Education, Madhya Bharat, Gwalior”.The complainant – senior Congress leader Chandra Shekhar Sinha, who is contesting the upcoming civic body elections from Ward 17 of Kailashahar Municipal Council – placed 16 documents before the court questioning the existence of that board. According to the court’s August 6, 2026, order, the record includes a list of fake educational boards published by the Madhya Pradesh government, a confidential letter dated July 9, 2019 (Letter No. 3395) from the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in Dehradun, and three communications from Assam government education and political authorities between August 2019 and November 20, 2025. Following a 2017 Allahabad High Court order, the CBI had investigated the Gwalior-based board as a fake entity and warned state governments in 2019 against certificates issued under its name.Addressing a press conference in Kailashahar on November 17, complainant’s counsel Advocate Narasingha Das said the CBI’s inquiry report had clearly stated that no such board existed. He also claimed that Roy’s Class 10 (Madhyamik) qualification was “under a question mark”.Clarifying that remark to The Wire on November 21, Das said, “We are receiving information that his madhyamik qualification is also fake. If we find preliminary merit in these claims, we will pursue that as well.”Months without an FIRThe road to the November 16, 2026, FIR order was marked by months of delay at the local police level. Sinha first submitted his complaint and supporting documents to Kailashahar police station on December 9, 2025, and later wrote to the Unakoti District Superintendent of Police on January 21, 2026. When no FIR was registered, he moved the court on April 17, 2026, in Case No. CR 25 of 2026.When the court sought an explanation, Kailashahar police station officials submitted a report on September 15, 2026, claiming they had already conducted “preliminary scrutiny and verification” of the complaint and informed Sinha on December 23, 2025 (Despatch No. 12644) that they would not register an FIR.Magistrate Ranjabati Roy asked the police to produce proof that Sinha had received this notice. In a follow-up report on October 7, 2026 (Despatch No. 14072), police said the inquiry had been handled by Sub-Inspector Ujjal Choudhury, who “inadvertently misplaced” the acknowledgment receipt while transferring from Kailashahar police station to Sepahijala district. Police requested the court to excuse what they called an unintentional, first-time lapse.Advocate Das questioned the police’s claim of having carried out any prior inquiry. “They claimed in their written report that they had conducted an inquiry, but they submitted no supporting documents to back it up,” Das told The Wire.The legal objections that failed to stop the FIRSetting aside the disputed claim over the missing receipt without ruling on it, Magistrate Roy dealt directly with the three legal objections raised by police to block an FIR. Police had argued that Section 215 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) barred action because the affidavit was filed before a Returning Officer, that a private citizen had no standing to file a case under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and that Section 125A was a non-cognizable offence.In her November 16 order, the magistrate, after considering the police’s submissions, rejected all three objections. Referring to her August 6 order, she noted that the allegations concerned Roy’s actions as an election candidate rather than his official duties as an MLA or minister, meaning the special legal protection for public servants under Section 175(4) of the BNSS did not apply.While agreeing that filing a false election affidavit under Section 125A is non-cognizable on its own, she pointed out that the complaint went further by alleging that Roy possessed and used forged educational certificates during the nomination process. Treating that as a separate cognizable offence, she ruled that under Section 174(4) of the BNSS, the entire case must be investigated as cognizable. She also noted that since the alleged acts took place before July 1, 2024, criminal liability would have to be examined under the law in force at that time, subject to Section 358 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.On the police’s objection to a private complainant, the magistrate cited the Supreme Court’s October 16, 2026 judgment in Rajkumar Madki v. Dr. Shailendra Beldale, which overturned the Karnataka high court ruling the police had relied on and held that a private complaint under Section 125A is not barred by Section 195 of the CrPC. Das also relied on an Election Commission of India instruction dated April 26, 2014, arguing that any individual could complain about a false election affidavit. The magistrate’s November 16 order records that he submitted a copy to the court.Clarifying that Section 215 of the BNSS only restricts a court from taking cognizance and does not stop a police probe, she also cited Om Prakash Ambadkar v. State of Maharashtra to note that a police investigation was necessary because key records lie with public and election authorities beyond a private citizen’s reach.At the same time, Roy added an explicit caveat. She wrote that the court “neither accepts the allegation that the documents are forged nor records any finding that the proposed accused had knowledge of their alleged falsity,” and passed the direction “without expressing any opinion regarding the truth of the allegations”.Congress flags 2023 nomination, eyes CBI probeBehind the courtroom battle lies a sharp political shift in Tripura ahead of the state’s civic polls. Records regarding Roy’s Gwalior certificate were first raised in May 2023 by TIPRA Motha Party candidate Ranjan Sinha, who demanded Roy’s disqualification. The party later joined the BJP-led state government in March 2024.Speaking to The Wire on Saturday, November 21, senior Congress leader and MLA Birajit Sinha said his party had flagged the issue the very day Roy filed his nomination in 2023. “We spotted the errors the very day he filed his nomination. Within an hour, we wrote to the Election Commission and the Returning Officer seeking the cancellation of his nomination for violating election rules, and we raised the objection again during scrutiny,” Sinha said.He added, “The Election Commission told us the Returning Officer would look into it, but the SDM acting as Returning Officer was biased towards the ruling party and refused to cancel it.”Explaining why Ranjan Sinha’s 2023 challenge did not move forward, Birajit Sinha said an election petition must be filed within 45 days and that Ranjan Sinha’s lawyer failed to submit it within that window. “We did not file an election petition. This is a criminal case,” Sinha said, claiming that the sections invoked in the complaint carry a punishment of up to 12 years in prison.Asked whether political pressure was behind the police’s reluctance to register an FIR, Sinha declined to speculate. “I cannot say whether there was political pressure or not. The law will take its own course,” he said.However, Sinha warned that the Congress would not wait indefinitely if the local investigation stalled. “If the lower court proceedings are delayed, we will file a writ petition in the high court seeking a CBI inquiry. The records have already been sent to an Advocate-on-Record at the Supreme Court for preparation. Let us see what report the police submit,” he told The Wire.The criminal case Roy allegedly left out of his affidavitApart from the educational certificate, the complaint also accuses Roy of concealing a pending criminal case in his 2023 election affidavit. This refers to West Agartala police station Case No. 154 of 2021, registered on the basis of an FIR lodged by Anal Roy Chowdhury, editor of the Tripura-based Bengali daily Pratibadi Kalam.Das told The Wire that the 2021 case remains unresolved. “Yes, that case is still under investigation. But now that he is a minister, how far will the probe really go? They will simply leave it as it is,” Das said.While Roy’s November 16 directive to register an FIR rests specifically on the cognizable forgery allegation rather than non-disclosure alone, all eyes are now on Kailashahar police station ahead of the next court date on December 17, 2026, to see whether the court’s order finally reaches the station and sets an investigation in motion.

headline: BJP MLA Rekha Patra off ventilator after suspected herbal larvicide poisoning
content: BJP MLA Rekha Patra was taken off ventilator support on Monday morning as doctors assessed whether she could breathe without assistance, news agency Press Trust of India reported. She is being treated following suspected poisoning and has shown signs of improvement.Patra has started responding and is doing better than before, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said after she and West Bengal Health Minister Sharadwat Mukhopadhyay spoke to doctors. "Rekha is better than before. She has been taken off the ventilator," Mukhopadhyay told reporters.According to PTI, Patra, the MLA from Hingalganj in West Bengal's North 24 Parganas district, developed complications after saliva accumulated in her mouth and entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply. The condition was detected during a CT scan of her chest and brought under control with antibiotics, Majumdar said."There is still some effect of the poison, due to which her heart rate is higher than normal. However, her kidneys have not been affected, which is a positive sign. Her potassium level was slightly elevated but is now under control," Majumdar said.She said doctors would observe Patra for another four days before determining whether she was out of danger. Her condition has shown encouraging improvement so far. A kidney specialist and a poisoning specialist were among the doctors who examined her.Sources said Patra suddenly fell ill at her residence in Hingalganj around 9 pm on Saturday. She was first taken to a local hospital and later shifted to Basirhat Super Speciality Hospital after preliminary treatment.She remained at the Basirhat hospital for nearly four hours before being referred to a hospital in Kolkata as her condition had not improved significantly. Her referral card said family members had reported that she had consumed a poisonous substance described as a "herbal larvicide".At the time of referral, Patra's blood pressure was 12470 mmHg and her pulse rate was 110 beats per minute. She required oxygen support at four litres per minute.Doctors also found her drowsy and barely responsive to calls. Attempts to wake her by applying pressure to her chest did not produce a significant response, leading to her transfer to Kolkata.At the Basirhat hospital, doctors administered medicines and injections to counter the suspected poisoning. She was given six activated charcoal tablets, and a tube was inserted through her nose to remove the toxic substance from her stomach.Patra has since been taken off ventilator support and is responding to treatment, but doctors will continue to monitor her for four more days before deciding whether she is out of danger.- EndsMust Watch

headline: ED summons Dharamkot AAP MLA, family members in money laundering probe against Moga legislator
content: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has summoned AAP MLA Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose, several serving and retired Punjab government officials and family members of Moga MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora for questioning in a money laundering probe against the woman legislator.The agency has asked Dhose, who represents Dharamkot, to appear at its Chandigarh zonal office on November 27, officials said. Kaur Arora (42) and her husband Rakesh Arora have also been summoned to depose on November 26 and 25, respectively.The ED has further summoned Kaur Arora's father Jaspal Singh, brother Valjinder Singh and maternal uncle Harminder Singh on November 27, November 30 and December 2, respectively.Among the government officials called for questioning are Moga District Revenue Officer Gurdev Singh Dham, Patwari Nirvair Singh and former Moga Tehsildar Lakhwinder Singh Gill. A man named Lakhwinder, a partner and director of a hospital-cum-de-addiction centre linked to the MLA, has also been asked to appear on Monday.The probe pertains to the alleged siphoning of compensation funds paid to residents of Moga district for land acquired to construct National Highway 754A.The ED case stems from an FIR registered by Moga Police at Dharamkot police station over alleged manipulation of revenue records relating to government land in Adhraman village. The manipulation allegedly led to the wrongful disbursement of more than Rs 1 crore in compensation.Following searches at her premises earlier this month, the ED alleged that Kaur Arora and her husband facilitated the diversion of the compensation funds.Kaur Arora, however, accused the BJP of political vendetta, claiming that during the 42-hour searches at her residence, the ED officials repeatedly pressured her to join the BJP in return for a ministerial position.She also claimed that the searches at her residence and hospital yielded no cash or other incriminating material.The AAP Women's Wing president in Punjab has been renominated by the party from Moga for the Assembly elections expected early next year.(With inputs from PTI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: “Talks will go smoothly, no differences of opinion over seat-sharing”: SP MP Awadhesh Prasad ahead of discussions with Congress
content: New Delhi [India], November 23 (ANI): Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Awadhesh Prasad on Monday expressed confidence that seat-sharing talks with the Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections would proceed smoothly, saying there were no differences between the two parties.Speaking to ANI in Delhi, Prasad said, "The talks will go well. There is no conflict of any kind between the two parties over seat-sharing, and there are no differences of opinion".The SP and Congress are holding their first round of seat-sharing discussions for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections at the residence of Congress leader Pramod Tiwari in New Delhi.The two-day meeting, scheduled for November 23 and 24, will see senior leaders from both parties participate in discussions on a possible seat-sharing arrangement ahead of the polls in the state, which has 403 Assembly constituencies.The SP delegation includes National General Secretary Ram Gopal Yadav, Uttar Pradesh unit president Shyam Lal Pal, and MPs Iqra Hasan and Rajiv Rai.According to sources, this is the first meeting between the two parties specifically concerning the upcoming Assembly elections, with discussions set to continue over two days.The talks come after the Samajwadi Party announced the formation of a committee to negotiate seat-sharing arrangements with its INDIA bloc partners for the 2027 polls.The Congress has also maintained that it intends to contest the Assembly elections to form the government in Uttar Pradesh. Party leader Aradhana Mishra had earlier said that strengthening the organisation was her primary priority and that the INDIA bloc would work towards securing victory in the state.The SP is seeking a major political comeback in 2027 after consecutive defeats in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections.In the 2022 Assembly elections, which the two parties contested separately, the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested, while the Congress secured two of the 399 seats on which it fielded candidates.However, the parties recorded a stronger performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, which they contested together under the INDIA bloc banner. The SP won 37 of the 62 seats it contested, while the Congress secured six of the 17 seats it contested.Uttar Pradesh, which has 403 Assembly seats, is expected to witness a major contest between the BJP and the SP in 2027, while the Congress is also seeking to expand its political footprint in the state. (ANI)

headline: ED summons AAP MLA, family members in probe against Moga legislator Amandeep Kaur Arora
content: Chandigarh The Enforcement Directorate has summoned the AAP MLA from Dharamkot, some serving and retired Punjab government officials and family members of Moga MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora in a money laundering probe against the woman legislator. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ PTI had earlier reported that Ms. Kaur Arora (42) and her husband Rakesh Arora have been summoned by the federal probe agency to depose at its Chandigarh zonal office for questioning on November 26 and November 25, respectively. After searches were conducted against Ms. Kaur Arora earlier this month, the ED issued a statement and alleged that she and her husband facilitated the siphoning of compensation funds the government gave to locals in Moga district whose land was acquired for constructing a highway. The ED case stems from an FIR filed by Moga Police (Dharamkot police station) on charges of manipulating revenue records of government land in Adhraman village, which resulted in the wrongful disbursement of more than ₹1 crore for the land acquired for the construction of National Highway No 754A. Officials said the agency has called Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose, MLA from Dharamkot, for questioning in the case against Ms. Kaur Arora on November 27. Ms. Kaur Arora's father, Jaspal Singh, brother Valjinder Singh and maternal uncle, Harminder Singh, have been asked to depose on November 27, November 30 and December 2, respectively. Moga District Revenue Officer (DRO) Gurdev Singh Dham, local Patwari Nirvair Singh and former Moga district Tehsildar Lakhwinder Singh Gill have also been summoned to unearth the alleged conspiracy, they said. A man named Lakhwinder, a partner and director in a hospital-cum-de-addiction centre linked to Ms. Kaur Arora, has been summoned to appear on Monday at the ED office, the officials said. After the raids, Ms. Kaur Arora accused the BJP of indulging in a political vendetta, alleging that the 42-hour-long ED raids at her residence included repeated pressure to join the BJP in exchange for a ministerial position. In an interaction with reporters, Ms. Kaur Arora claimed that despite extensive searches at her residence and hospital, the ED could not recover a single penny and returned empty-handed. Kaur Arora, who is also the president of the AAP Women's Wing in Punjab, has been renominated by the party from the Moga seat for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year.

headline: 'Why remove mata Sita's name?' Congress slams BJP over 'Jai Shri Ram' remark
content: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Ajay Rai on Sunday criticised Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks on the slogans 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Radhe Radhe', accusing the BJP leader of having a "perverted mindset" for dropping the name of Goddess Sita from the traditional greeting."This reflects the perverted mindset of Keshav Prasad Maurya. These are people with a perverted mindset. No one has any problem with the original phrasing. Previously, instead of 'Jai Shri Ram', the phrase used was 'Jai Siya Ram'—but these people have even removed the name of Mother Sita..." Rai said.His remarks came amid a war of words between Maurya and Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over the BJP's slogan, 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' (May the lotus bloom).On Sunday, Maurya took a swipe at the SP, saying its leaders had earlier felt uneasy hearing 'Jai Shri Ram' and were now troubled even by the chant of 'Radhe Radhe'.In a post on X, Maurya said, “SP leaders earlier felt uneasy hearing ‘Jai Shri Ram’. Now they are troubled even by ‘Radhe Radhe’.”“In Ayodhya, ‘Jai Shri Ram’ resonates, while in Braj people greet each other by saying ‘Radhe Radhe’,” he said.Asking Yadav to clarify his position, the deputy chief minister said, “Does this mean people in Uttar Pradesh will now have to seek his permission before taking the name of their deity?”Maurya accused the SP of indulging in appeasement politics and said both ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Radhe Radhe’ would continue to resonate in Uttar Pradesh. He also claimed that the party's hopes of returning to power in the 2027 Assembly elections would be dashed and that the BJP would form the government again.The exchange followed Yadav's remarks on Saturday, when he mocked the BJP's slogan during a press conference at the party headquarters in Lucknow.Referring to the slogan coined after the BJP's two-day meeting in Mathura, the former chief minister said the party was aware that its lotus symbol was wilting and was therefore chanting 'Radhe Radhe'.“‘Radhe Radhe’ is said at the time of farewell in our tradition. It means the BJP is going to be shown the door,” Yadav had said, claiming that the people of Uttar Pradesh would give the party a “grand farewell” in the coming elections.On Sunday, responding to Maurya's remarks, Yadav said, "I would never invite him to my house in my lifetime. But you (reporter) are welcome to visit our house; we will show you 'Radhe Radhe'.""'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' go ahead and make it bloom. Does it mean the lotus has withered? Why do you (BJP) need to make it bloom again? It has withered," he said at a press conference.Yadav also accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, clarifying that his party was not opposed to 'katha' (religious discourses) but objected to controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram and what was said about our Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme," he said without naming anyone."Can you make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? Tell me, what would happen if someone among us made such a statement?" he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Congress Slams BRS Over Warangal Development Claims
content: Hyderabad: Congress MLAs Nayini Rajender Reddy, KR Nagaraju and MP K Kavya strongly criticised the previous BRS government, questioning its achievements during its ten-year rule. Speaking to media persons, Rajender Reddy dismissed the recent remarks made by BRS working president KT Rama Rao (KTR) during his visit to Warangal, describing them as misleading and far from the truth. He alleged that BRS leaders were making false claims about the city's development while ignoring the unfulfilled promises made during BRS tenure. Rajender Reddy questioned what the BRS government had actually achieved for Warangal during its rule. Referring to BRS’s past promises and videos highlighting alleged unfulfilled assurances, he challenged BRS leaders to explain their development to the people. The Congress MLA stated that the present Congress government had completed the long-pending Kaloji Kalakshetra project in Warangal. He also alleged that some BRS leaders were now taking credit for development works undertaken by the previous government without presenting the complete facts. Reacting to the Warangal airport issue, Rajender Reddy said that the Congress government had completed the land acquisition process for the proposed airport. He asserted that the current government was committed to taking forward development projects in the region. Rajender Reddy challenged BRS leaders to participate in an open debate on Warangal's development at any major public junction in Hanamkonda. He said he was ready to discuss the development works undertaken by both governments and asked why the BRS had lost the people's mandate despite claiming to have developed Warangal during its ten-year rule.

headline: “TVK govt has hurt sentiments of Tamil Nadu people”: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan slams state govt over Karthigai Deepam review plea
content: Hyderabad (Telangana) [India], November 23 (ANI): BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan on Monday strongly criticised the Tamil Nadu government for filing a review petition in the Supreme Court against its order permitting the lighting of Karthigai Deepam at Deepathoon on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai on November 24, accusing the ruling TVK-Congress government of hurting the sentiments of Hindu devotees and indulging in vote-bank politics.Kesavan described the state government's decision to challenge the Supreme Court's directive as regressive and alleged that it had insulted the faith of crores of Hindu devotees.Speaking to ANI, he said, "The highly regressive decision of the TVK Congress government led by Joseph Vijay to hurriedly file a review petition against the Supreme Court's directive to allow limited lighting of the sacred Karthegai Deepam at the Deepathoon atop the sacred Thiruparankundram hill has deeply hurt the self-respect and blatantly insulted the faith of crores of Hindu devotees."Accusing the state government of following what he described as appeasement politics, Kesavan said the TVK-Congress government was acting in a manner like the DMK government."This opportunistic TVK Congress government comes across as a carbon copy, an ideological twin when it comes to blatantly attacking and assaulting Hindu faith to perpetrate a bigoted vote bank politics of appeasement," he said.Kesavan further alleged that the government's move had triggered widespread anger in Tamil Nadu and warned that the ruling alliance would face the people's response."The TVK Congress government has really hurt the sentiments of the Tamil Nadu people, and there is widespread backlash and anger over the TVK and Congress government's dangerous and divisive politics of polarisation. Like the people of Tamil Nadu taught a fitting lesson to the erstwhile DMK government, the TVK Congress regime will be taught a fitting lesson by the people of Tamil Nadu and eventually justice will prevail, and the implicit faith of crores of Lord Muruga devotees will eventually triumph," he added.The dispute concerns the annual lighting of Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah in Madurai.The controversy began in November 2025, when local authorities withheld permission for the hilltop ritual, citing law-and-order concerns and the site's proximity to the dargah.In December 2025, a single judge of the Madras High Court directed the temple authorities to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, observing that the pillar was situated more than 50 metres from the dargah. A division bench upheld the direction on January 6, 2026, while requiring the temple administration to coordinate the ritual with the police and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), considering the site's heritage status.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently challenged the High Court's decisions before the Supreme Court, which issued notice on the state's plea in August 2026.On November 20, a Supreme Court bench led by Justice Aravind Kumar permitted a strictly conditional, one-time lighting of the lamp on November 24. The order did not establish a legal precedent or settle the broader claims relating to ownership and customary rights.The Tamil Nadu government has since filed a review petition seeking an immediate stay on the Supreme Court's order. (ANI)

headline: Minister alleges political backing for Messi event deal, says probe will expose those responsible
content: Thrissur , Sports Minister O J Janeesh on Monday alleged that the irregularities in the failed visit of the Lionel Messi-led Argentina football team to Keralam during the previous LDF government were politically driven, and that the SIT probe is in the right direction.After the UDF government came to power, it constituted a Special Investigation Team to probe the irregularities.The SIT on Saturday named former Sports Minister V Abdurahiman, his former private secretary C Sathyapalan and former Kerala State Sports Council president U Sharafali as accused in the case.The SIT had earlier registered the case against the sponsoring company and its managing director.Sharafali had claimed that his football academy in Malappuram received a ₹2 crore investment from the company that sponsored the Messi event.Speaking to reporters, Janeesh said the SIT probing alleged irregularities in the event was progressing in the right direction and would bring out who was behind the decisions that led to the agreement."It was not something that happened solely because a Sports Council president wanted it or because the Sports Minister's office decided so. There was political ownership behind the agreement. Who provided that political ownership will come out clearly in the investigation," he said.He said the previous government's political leadership had a responsibility in the matter, as former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan had repeatedly announced that Messi would visit Keralam and assured people that the event would take place.Such assurances had created confidence among those willing to invest money in the event and facilitated the financial transactions, he said.Janeesh said the issue was not merely whether the government had suffered a direct financial loss. "The government machinery was fully utilised for this. The time of senior officials and the government system was devoted to the event. That itself amounts to a loss to the government," he said.He said the most important question was whether the government machinery had been used to facilitate private financial transactions.If such misuse had taken place, everyone who had assisted in it should come within the scope of the investigation, he said.The minister also referred to allegations against Sharafali, whose sports academy reportedly received ₹2 crore as an investment from the sponsor of the proposed event.Janeesh said Sharafali had allegedly signed an agreement between the sponsor and an international agency to organise the Messi event even before the state government granted approval.The agreement was reportedly signed two days before the government approval, with Sharafali signing in his official capacity as Sports Council president, he said.He said money was subsequently transferred to an account linked to Sharafali's institution and was allegedly moved to other accounts.Janeesh said the circumstances surrounding the agreement and the financial transactions warranted a detailed investigation.He maintained that the government had not interfered in the probe and called for a transparent and effective investigation.He rejected the Opposition's allegation that the investigation was being delayed, saying the matter required careful examination and could not be concluded in a week merely to satisfy public sentiment.Janeesh also said the Sports Department's report had pointed to inadequate preparations, shortcomings in the movement of files, and misuse of government machinery.He said that the lack of transparency surrounding the arrangements was one of the reasons for initiating an SIT investigation.He said the SIT should examine the allegations and counter-arguments and that the investigation should establish the political and administrative responsibility for the decisions and transactions linked to the failed event.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

headline: ED summons AAP MLA, family members in probe against Moga legislator Amandeep Kaur Arora
content: Chandigarh The Enforcement Directorate has summoned the AAP MLA from Dharamkot, some serving and retired Punjab government officials and family members of Moga MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora in a money laundering probe against the woman legislator. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ PTI had earlier reported that Ms. Kaur Arora (42) and her husband Rakesh Arora have been summoned by the federal probe agency to depose at its Chandigarh zonal office for questioning on November 26 and November 25, respectively. After searches were conducted against Ms. Kaur Arora earlier this month, the ED issued a statement and alleged that she and her husband facilitated the siphoning of compensation funds the government gave to locals in Moga district whose land was acquired for constructing a highway. The ED case stems from an FIR filed by Moga Police (Dharamkot police station) on charges of manipulating revenue records of government land in Adhraman village, which resulted in the wrongful disbursement of more than ₹1 crore for the land acquired for the construction of National Highway No 754A. Officials said the agency has called Devinderjeet Singh Laddi Dhose, MLA from Dharamkot, for questioning in the case against Ms. Kaur Arora on November 27. Ms. Kaur Arora's father, Jaspal Singh, brother Valjinder Singh and maternal uncle, Harminder Singh, have been asked to depose on November 27, November 30 and December 2, respectively. Moga District Revenue Officer (DRO) Gurdev Singh Dham, local Patwari Nirvair Singh and former Moga district Tehsildar Lakhwinder Singh Gill have also been summoned to unearth the alleged conspiracy, they said. A man named Lakhwinder, a partner and director in a hospital-cum-de-addiction centre linked to Ms. Kaur Arora, has been summoned to appear on Monday at the ED office, the officials said. After the raids, Ms. Kaur Arora accused the BJP of indulging in a political vendetta, alleging that the 42-hour-long ED raids at her residence included repeated pressure to join the BJP in exchange for a ministerial position. In an interaction with reporters, Ms. Kaur Arora claimed that despite extensive searches at her residence and hospital, the ED could not recover a single penny and returned empty-handed. Kaur Arora, who is also the president of the AAP Women's Wing in Punjab, has been renominated by the party from the Moga seat for the Punjab Assembly elections expected early next year.

headline: Service Tax Not Payable on Goods Supplied Under Composite Government Contracts: CESTAT Chandigarh
content:
Summary : Summary: The Chandigarh Bench of the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), in five connected appeals filed by M/s National Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Engg., set aside service tax demands aggregating to ₹1,25,43,246 and penalties aggregating to ₹1,92,63,601 imposed in relation to composite contracts for supplying air-conditioning machinery, equipment and parts, together with erection, commissioning, installation and associated civil works. The appellant executed contracts for Government departments and authorities, including the Military Engineering Services (MES), Ordnance Factories, Railways, Airports, Government hospitals and the State of Jammu & Kashmir. The contracts specified the machinery and materials to be supplied, while the appellant paid VAT/CST on materials and the recipients deducted works contract tax. The five appeals covered different periods, including October 2003 to September 2008, 2010–11 and 2013–14. The principal appeal concerned a demand of ₹73,15,931, besides interest and penalties under Sections 76, 77 and 78 of the Finance Act, 1994.

In the first round of litigation, CESTAT, by Final Order No. ST/158/2011-Cus DB dated 24 February 2011, had remanded the matter after observing that the adjudicating authority had not properly examined the work orders, particularly the separate labour charges for erection, commissioning and testing. The Tribunal had also considered the Military Engineering Services letter dated 20 February 2008, which reproduced a Ministry of Finance clarification concerning repair and maintenance services connected with buildings or civil structures not used for commercial activities. It had specifically observed that services rendered to MES during the relevant period were not liable to service tax, that the appellant was entitled to cum-service-tax benefit where applicable, and that the taxable value had to be examined with reference to the labour charges for erection, installation and commissioning. However, the adjudicating authority, through its order dated 1 October 2012, substantially reiterated its earlier demand of ₹73,15,931 and imposed penalties, taking the view that the 5% labour component mentioned in one work order did not represent the entire service portion of the composite contracts.

The appellant contended that the adjudicating authority had exceeded the scope of remand and disregarded the Tribunal’s earlier directions. It produced a Chartered Accountant’s certificate and supporting contracts showing aggregate receipts of ₹19,90,42,973 during October 2003 to September 2008. Of this amount, ₹16,35,58,494 represented the supply of goods, ₹54,22,876 related to civil works, ₹50,58,543 represented services rendered, and ₹2,50,03,060 related to work executed in Jammu & Kashmir. The certificate further identified receipts of ₹14,00,54,298 from MES, ₹1,96,39,742 from Ordnance Factory, ₹32,13,165 from Railways, ₹12,32,077 from Airports and ₹99,00,630 from Government hospitals. The appellant argued that the goods component had been subjected to VAT/sales tax and could not again be included in the service-tax value; services rendered to MES and Government bodies were not taxable or were exempt; services performed in Jammu & Kashmir were outside the relevant levy; and the amount of ₹50,58,543 shown as service receipts had already suffered service tax. It also disputed the application of the 67% abatement method under Notifications Nos. 19/2003-ST dated 21 August 2003 and 1/2006-ST dated 1 March 2006, maintaining that the actual value of goods and services was identifiable from the contracts.

The Revenue defended the adjudication by relying on the composite nature of the contracts and the fact that several work orders separately mentioned supervision, erection, commissioning and testing charges. It argued that the service component could not be restricted to the 5% labour charge in one particular work order, since the value of service also included supervision, testing at different stages, erection and other related expenses. The adjudicating authority had also rejected the MES clarification on the ground that it concerned repair and maintenance services rather than erection, commissioning, installation or works contract services. On valuation, it relied on Section 67 of the Finance Act, 1994, Notification No. 19/2003-ST and Rule 2A of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006, taking the position that the value of the taxable service included labour, subcontractor charges, planning and designing, machinery hire, consumables, establishment expenses and profit attributable to labour and services. The appellant separately challenged the extended limitation period, alleging absence of wilful suppression or intent to evade tax, and disputed simultaneous penalties under Sections 76 and 78.

CESTAT examined the actual receipts and documentary evidence, including the Chartered Accountant’s certificate and contracts placed in Annexure D of the appeal paper book. It noted that the Commissioner had allowed a notional 67% deduction towards goods from the gross receipts, whereas the appellant had produced evidence identifying the actual goods component of ₹16,35,58,494. Relying on Commissioner of Central Excise & Customs, Kerala Vs Larsen & Toubro Ltd., 2015 (39) S.T.R. 913 (S.C.), the Tribunal held that the goods portion, where identifiable and subjected to sales tax, could not be subjected to service tax through a notional valuation. It further noted that works contract service became taxable only from 1 June 2007 and that, before the introduction of a specific charging provision for works contracts, indivisible composite contracts could not be subjected to service tax under the earlier taxable-service entries. The Tribunal also accepted the appellant’s submissions concerning services rendered to Government authorities and departments, the exempt nature of work performed in Jammu & Kashmir, and the exclusion of the goods component. It distinguished the MES clarification issue from the separate question of taxability under erection, commissioning and installation services, while ultimately agreeing with the appellant on the relevant non-taxability claims.

On limitation and penalties, the Tribunal observed that the legal position concerning composite and works contracts remained unsettled during the relevant period and was clarified by the Supreme Court in Larsen & Toubro. The show-cause notice for the principal period had been issued on 22 April 2009, invoking the extended period. In the circumstances, the appellant could not be said to have deliberately suppressed facts or intended to evade tax merely because of a disputed interpretation of the service-tax provisions. The Tribunal also considered that the supplies were predominantly made to Government departments and authorities and that the appellant was not shown to have deliberately enriched itself through tax evasion. It concluded that the demands were unsustainable on the facts and law and that the consequential penalties could not survive. Accordingly, all five appeals were allowed with consequential relief, by Final Order Nos. 60592–60596/2026 pronounced in open court on 4 November 2026.

headline: Top Telecom Operator Airtels Bharti Airtel Foundation Grants 55 Scholarships to Chandigarh Universitys Engineering Students
content: Bharti Airtel Scholarships Worth Over Rs 7 Crore to Cover 100% Tuition, Hostel and Mess Support for Deserving Chandigarh University Engineering Students from Diverse Socio-Economic BackgroundsCHANDIGARH, India, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As a part of its Institutional Social Responsibility (ISR), Chandigarh University has facilitated 55 scholarships, with cumulative scholarship and support corpus of Rs 7.7 Crore over four years, for its engineering students under the Bharti Airtel Scholarship Program of Bharti Airtel Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Bharti Enterprises, for the academic session 2026–27, the highest number of scholarships secured by any private university for the second consecutive year, reinforcing its commitment to expanding access to quality higher education through impactful corporate partnerships.The dignitaries who graced the Bharti Airtel Scholarship Investiture Ceremony included Sameer Shah, Head Higher Education and Strategic Relations at Bharti Airtel Foundation, Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal, Vice Chancellor, Chandigarh University, Namit Singh, Manager, Scholarship and Higher Education, Bharti Airtel Foundation, Pooja Satija, Manager, Higher Education, Scholarship & Mentorship, Bharti Airtel Foundation.Speaking on the occasion, Sameer Shah, Head Higher Education and Strategic Relations at Bharti Airtel Foundation, said, "Bharti Airtel Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Bharti Enterprises, had launched the Bharti Airtel Scholarship Program' in 2024 to support deserving students from diverse socio-economic backgrounds, with a particular emphasis on girl students, children with disability students who do not have parents or either are a single parent, in becoming future technology leaders. This merit-cum-means-based scholarship is designed for students seeking admission in the first year of undergraduate engineering and 5-year integrated technology courses at the top 50 National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) (Engineering) colleges, including Chandigarh University.""This scholarship covers 100% of annual tuition fee for the full duration of undergraduate and integrated courses. With 100% scholarship, we ensure that we not only selected students with tuition fee but we also provide them full coverage of hostel and mess fees for scholars residing in campus facilities. For scholars staying in private accommodations, support is extended equivalent to the institute's hostel or mess charges. Today we have handed over scholarships to 55 students of the Chandigarh University. High-end laptops worth over Rs 1.25 lakh and Airtel SIM card with complimentary services for four years have also been provided to each of these 55 scholars to aid in their studies. Currently, Bharti Airtel Foundation is providing such scholarships to about 1600 students in top higher educational institutions like in Chandigarh University which rank among the top 50 in the NIRF rankings," he said.Sameer Shah further said, "During the academic journey, Bharti Airtel Foundation will also help these students through mentorships, webinars and career talks. We recently also just launched a mentorship program with the help of Airtel leaders. Each leader is committing to support one such student through a guided mentorship. So objective is not to teach them their subjects but the objective is how can we make them future ready. So not only academics but they will also need skills like confidence, communication, collaboration, we will help them in this journey through mentorship and internships. To get internships, students will need skills and our objective is how do we prepare them for that so that they can get internships not just in Airtel but anywhere. We will provide the ecosystem for this."Earlier in his welcome address, Prof (Dr) SS Sehgal, Vice Chancellor, Chandigarh University said, "Chandigarh University has always strived to remove financial obstacles faced by meritorious and economically weaker students through Chandigarh University Common Entrance Test (CUCET) and other scholarship schemes worth Rs 250 Crore to encourage meritorious students to realise their dreams and pave the way for their bright future. We are proud to partner with Bharti Airtel Foundation in facilitating the Bharti Airtel Scholarship Program for Chandigarh University students, which has seen consistent growth in past three years. Starting with eight Scholarships under Bharti Airtel Scholarship Program in 2024–25, the number of these scholarships went up to 33 Scholarships in 2025–26. This academic year, the number of these scholarships to Chandigarh University students has gone up top 55, making CU the only private university to secure the highest number of scholarships for the last two consecutive academic sessions. This ISR initiative reflects Chandigarh University's commitment to identifying opportunities for deserving students, facilitating access to quality higher education, and building impactful corporate CSR partnerships. A proud ISR milestone that goes beyond scholarships, creating opportunities, enabling digital empowerment and transforming students' aspirations into reality."About Chandigarh UniversityChandigarh University is a NAAC A+ Grade University and QS World Ranked University. This autonomous educational institution is approved by UGC and is located near Chandigarh in the state of Punjab. It is the youngest university in India and the only private university in Punjab to be honoured with A+ Grade by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council). CU offers more than 109 UG and PG programs in the field of engineering, management, pharmacy, law, architecture, journalism, animation, hotel management, commerce, and others. It has been awarded as The University with Best Placements by WCRC.Website address: https://www.cuchd.in/(Disclaimer: The above press release comes to you under an arrangement with PRNewswire and PTI takes no editorial responsibility for the same.). headline: Nitin Nabin sounds poll bugle in Chandigarh, tells BJP workers to avenge 2024 LS poll defeat
content: Sounding the poll bugle for the Municipal Corporation elections, BJP national president Nitin Nabin today called upon party workers to avenge the party’s defeat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections by securing a decisive victory in Chandigarh in 2026.Addressing a booth-level workers’ conference in Sector 27, Nabin urged party workers to strengthen their grassroots presence, overcome internal differences and reach out to every household with the achievements of the Narendra Modi government and the Chandigarh Administration.He said BJP workers were not part-time politicians but dedicated party members who remained connected with people throughout the year. He asked them to identify the shortcomings of previous elections, address public grievances and present the party’s development report card before voters.Nabin also asked Chandigarh BJP president Jatinder Pal Malhotra and his team to prepare a comprehensive development roadmap for the city and approach voters with a clear vision and manifesto.Describing Chandigarh as a “Mini India”, he said people from different states, religions, languages and communities lived together in harmony, reflecting the country’s cultural diversity and unity.Taking a dig at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, Nabin said even a BJP mandal president was capable of countering his arguments. He accused the Congress of being more concerned about its family and political interests than the country’s development. He also alleged that some Opposition leaders made statements abroad that tarnished India’s image.Defending the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Nabin accused the Opposition of misleading people by raising allegations of vote theft. He said removing the names of deceased persons, duplicate voters and ineligible entries was necessary to maintain the integrity of the electoral rolls. He urged party workers to visit households, identify such entries and share the information with the Election Commission.Highlighting the achievements of the Modi government, Nabin said India had made significant progress in economic growth and global recognition under the Prime Minister’s leadership. Referring to Modi’s 25 years in public life as head of governments, he said the country had emerged as the world’s fourth-largest economy.He said more than two lakh startups were operating in the country and young people were increasingly becoming job creators rather than merely job seekers.He said the government had ensured that benefits reached people directly through their bank accounts, eliminating middlemen.On women’s empowerment, Nabin said the government had taken several steps to ensure women’s dignity, safety and economic independence. He referred to the Swachh Bharat Mission and the Lakhpati Didi initiative, saying that these would strengthen women’s participation in the country’s development. He added that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam would be implemented soon to strengthen women’s representation in decision-making.Emphasising national security, he said the Modi government had strengthened the armed forces and India’s ability to respond to challenges along its borders. He also referred to the government’s approach of developing border villages as the country’s first villages rather than its last.Taking aim at AAP, Nabin said that after defeating the party in Delhi, the BJP would work towards defeating it in Chandigarh and subsequently strengthening its position in Punjab.

headline: Uttar Pradesh’s higher education transformation since 2017: Expansion, quality, skills and innovation
content: The Uttar Pradesh government under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has undertaken a major expansion of the higher education sector since 2017, with an emphasis on increasing institutional capacity, improving academic standards, adopting technology and connecting education with employment.Over the past nine years, Uttar Pradesh has sought to move beyond the traditional approach of expanding access to degrees. Its higher education strategy increasingly focuses on multidisciplinary learning, research, innovation, industry partnerships and skill development. The expansion of universities and colleges, the introduction of National Education Policy 2020 reforms, greater use of digital learning and new opportunities for women and disadvantaged sections are important elements of this transformation.The scale of institutional growth is particularly significant. Government universities, private universities and colleges have all expanded, creating a wider network of educational opportunities across the state.A major expansion of universities and collegesOne of the most visible changes since 2017 has been the expansion of Uttar Pradesh's university network. Before 2017, the state had 16 government universities. Three additional government universities were established between 2017 and 2022, followed by five more after 2022. With the inclusion of a deemed university and an open university, the number of government-sector university institutions has reached 26, according to the figures provided.Private universities have recorded even faster growth. Their number has increased from 26 to 56, more than doubling the private university network. Significantly, 27 private universities have been established after 2022, reflecting growing interest among educational institutions and investors in Uttar Pradesh's higher education sector.This expansion is important because it increases the geographical availability of higher education and gives students more choices in terms of courses, specialisations and academic environments. It also reduces the pressure on established universities and creates opportunities for students who might otherwise have to move to other states for higher studies.The opening of off-campus centres of a couple of Universities in Noida is another development. It reflects the growing importance of the National Capital Region as an education and employment hub.The Higher Education Promotion Policy-2024 has also been introduced to encourage private universities to establish institutions in districts where access to higher education remains comparatively limited.The growth of colleges has been equally substantial. Government colleges have increased from 158 to 261, an expansion of approximately 65 per cent. The number of self-financed colleges has risen from 6,681 to 8,030, an increase of around 20 per cent.Taken together, the number of government and self-financed colleges has increased from 6,839 to 8,291. This represents an addition of 1,452 colleges, or approximately 21 per cent, to the higher education network.This expansion has a direct bearing on access. More colleges mean more local opportunities for undergraduate education, particularly for students from rural areas, economically weaker families and smaller towns. It can also reduce travel and accommodation expenses for families and make higher education more accessible to women.From institutional growth to greater student capacityThe increase in the number of institutions is an important indicator of progress, but its real significance lies in the additional opportunities created for students. Every new university and collegeexpands the potential capacity of the state to accommodate young people seeking undergraduate, postgraduate, professional and specialised education.The expansion is particularly important in a state as large and populous as Uttar Pradesh. For decades, students from smaller towns and rural districts often had to travel to major cities for higher education. The growth of colleges and universities is helping distribute educational infrastructure more widely across the state.Recent figures illustrate the scale of the student base. More than 53.28 lakh students enrolled in traditional higher education courses during 2024–25, including BA, BSc and BCom programmes. Of these, approximately 28.75 lakh were women and 24.54 lakh were men. Female enrolment exceeded male enrolment by more than 4.21 lakh, indicating the growing participation of women in higher education.For 2025–26, reported enrolment in traditional undergraduate courses stood at approximately 48.95 lakh across 8,072 colleges. The decline from the previous year's figure also highlights an important policy challenge: expanding the number of institutions must go hand in hand with improving enrolment, the relevance of courses and the quality of teaching.It is important to distinguish between student enrolment and sanctioned admission capacity. Enrolment tells us how many students actually entered courses, whereas intake capacity represents the number of seats institutions are authorised to offer. The two figures should not be treated as interchangeable.The available state-level institutional data also show that the expansion has continued beyond the figures for 2017–2026 in the original government account. A July 2026 report placed the number of state universities at 24, private universities at 56, and one each of deemed and open universities. It also reported 216 government colleges, 330 aided colleges and 7,526 self-financed colleges. This gives a total of 8,072 colleges across these three categories.The figures from different government and departmental reports use different institutional classifications and reporting dates. They should therefore be presented with their respective dates rather than combined as though they were one uniform statistical series.Improving quality and national recognitionExpansion alone cannot create a strong higher education system. The quality of teaching, research, infrastructure, faculty and institutional governance is equally important. Uttar Pradesh has therefore placed increasing emphasis on improving the academic standards of its universities and colleges.Seven institutions from the state have appeared in the NIRF rankings for the first time, while three universities have entered the country's top 100, according to the government information provided.The National Institutional Ranking Framework evaluates institutions on parameters including teaching and learning resources, research, graduation outcomes, outreach and perception. Greater participation in NIRF reflects an effort to make institutions more accountable for their academic performance and encourages them to compete nationally.A major investment has also come through the Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA). Uttar Pradesh has received Rs 965 crore from the Centre under the scheme, the highest allocation to any state, as stated in the government release. The funds are intended to strengthen infrastructure, laboratories, research facilities and smart classrooms.These investments are important because students need more than classroom teaching. Access to modern laboratories, libraries, digital resources and research facilities can improve learning outcomes and prepare graduates for an increasingly competitive employment market.Global partnerships and internationalisationUttar Pradesh is also seeking to establish itself as an international destination for higher education. The state has signed 776 agreements with national and international academic institutions to promote academic cooperation, research, faculty development, student exchange and institutional collaboration.A significant development is the proposal to establish a campus of Australia's Western Sydney University in Greater Noida. Such partnerships can bring international academic practices, specialised courses and research opportunities closer to students in the state. The presence of international institutions can also strengthen the connection between universities and industry. Students can gain exposure to global standards, while domestic institutions can benefit from collaborative research, faculty exchanges and access to international academic networks.The objective is to make Uttar Pradesh's higher education system more competitive and internationally connected.National Education Policy 2020: Changing the learning frameworkThe implementation of the National Education Policy 2020 has brought a major shift in the approach to higher education. The focus is moving from a rigid, subject-specific system towards flexible, multidisciplinary and outcome-oriented learning.Uttar Pradesh has introduced several important NEP provisions, including the Choice Based Credit System, multiple entry and exit options, multidisciplinary education and the integration of the Indian Knowledge System.The Choice Based Credit System gives students greater flexibility in selecting subjects and earning credits. Multiple entry and exit provisions are intended to ensure that students who cannot complete an entire programme at one time do not lose the academic progress they have already made.Multidisciplinary education allows students to combine subjects from different fields, helping them develop broader knowledge and problem-solving abilities. This is particularly relevant in a changing employment market where professionals increasingly need a combination of technical, analytical and communication skills.The state is also promoting traditional Indian knowledge through research chairs and academic initiatives. Sampurnanand Sanskrit University has established an online Sanskrit training centre, creating opportunities for students to learn the language and access traditional knowledge through digital platforms.These reforms seek to make higher education more inclusive, flexible and relevant to contemporaryTechnology-enabled learning and digital infrastructureTechnology has become another important pillar of the state's higher education strategy. Digital learning resources, smart classrooms and laboratories are being introduced to improve the quality and reach of education.According to the government figures, more than 88,532 e-content resources have been developed across 239 subjects. Government colleges have also been equipped with 251 smart classrooms, more than 83 smart laboratories and 171 e-learning parks.These facilities enable students to access digital study material, interactive teaching and technology-supported academic resources. They are particularly useful in institutions where access to specialised books, laboratories and other learning facilities may be limited.Artificial intelligence is also beginning to influence higher education. Chandigarh University, for example, has introduced AI-based learning across all 43 of its courses. Such initiatives demonstrate how universities can use technology to modernise teaching, improve learning experiences and prepare students for emerging professional requirements.The next stage of this transformation will depend on ensuring that digital facilities are not merely installed but regularly used, updated and made accessible to students from all economic backgrounds.Skill development: Connecting education with employmentA key objective of the higher education transformation is to ensure that academic qualifications translate into employment opportunities. The Uttar Pradesh Skill Development Mission has therefore emerged as an important complement to the university and college system.Since 2017–18, more than 17 lakh young people have received training through the mission, while over seven lakhs have secured employment. The government has also organised 1,194 mega employment fairs, through which 4,52,976 candidates have been placed.The state's performance in the India Skills Competition-2025 was another achievement. Uttar Pradesh secured the first position nationally with 1,09,249 registrations. It continued to lead with 1,07,464 registrations for 2026–27, according to the figures supplied.To align training with changing industry requirements, 82 New Age Training Partners have been associated with the mission. Agreements with premier institutions such as IIT Roorkee, MNNIT Prayagraj, IIIT Prayagraj and NIESBUD are facilitating specialised training in emerging fields.Digital platforms, including Kaushal Darpan, Kaushal Disha, Kaushal Drishti and Kaushal Dost, are being used to improve training delivery, monitoring and programme management.Special attention is also being given to employment opportunities for persons with disabilities. Government initiatives have helped 3,441 persons with disabilities secure jobs, supporting their economic independence and social inclusion.The broader objective is to create an integrated education-to-employment ecosystem in which universities, colleges, training institutions and industries work together.Empowering women through higher educationWomen's participation is an important indicator of the inclusiveness of an education system. Uttar Pradesh has introduced initiatives to encourage more female students to pursue higher education and achieve academic excellence.One of the notable decisions is to provide scooters to the top five per cent of female students, with approximately 40,000 students expected to benefit. The initiative is intended to encourage academic performance while addressing mobility challenges that sometimes prevent young women from pursuing higher education.The increasing participation of women is also reflected in enrolment figures. During 2024–25, female students accounted for approximately 28.75 lakh of the 53.28 lakh students enrolled in traditional higher education courses. Their number was more than four lakh higher than male enrolment.The government has also extended cashless medical facilities to more than 1.28 lakh people, including teachers and their dependents. Such welfare measures contribute to the security and well-being of the academic workforce.Beyond numbers to educational excellenceThe expansion of higher education in Uttar Pradesh since 2017 represents an important change in the state's educational landscape. The growth of universities and colleges, investments in infrastructure, digital learning facilities, international partnerships and skill-development initiatives have created a broader platform for educational advancement.However, the next phase must focus on ensuring that institutional expansion translates into higher student participation, better learning outcomes and stronger employment prospects.Three priorities will be particularly important: improving the quality of teaching and research, increasing access to specialised and professional courses, and ensuring that institutions in smaller towns and rural districts receive adequate faculty, laboratories, libraries and digital infrastructure.The state must also focus on increasing the Gross Enrolment Ratio, improving the utilisation of available seats and reducing the gap between sanctioned intake and actual admissions. The objective should be to ensure that every additional college and university contributes meaningfully to educational access.The Yogi government's stated vision is to transform Uttar Pradesh from a state where higher education was often associated primarily with obtaining degrees into one where universities become centres of knowledge, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and professional excellence.With a rapidly expanding institutional network and a growing emphasis on technology and employability, Uttar Pradesh is working towards building a higher education ecosystem capable of supporting its ambition of becoming a major knowledge-driven economy.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. headline: Education system must promote innovation, says Sukhu
content: Kullu: While extending best wishes to the students receiving degrees at the 10th convocation ceremony of Himachal Pradesh Central University, held in Dharamshala on Sunday, chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that a convocation ceremony is not merely a milestone in an academic journey but also marks the beginning of a new chapter in life.The CM said that in an era of rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, robotics, biotechnology, data science and digital technology, the education system must prepare young people not only to seek employment but also to generate employment, undertake research and promote innovation.He added that the state govt considers education a vital foundation for development and self-reliance. The govt's objective is to provide the youth of Himachal Pradesh with modern knowledge and technology and enable them to establish their identity at national and international levels. Considering the challenging geographical conditions of the state, he said that it is the govt's responsibility to ensure access to quality education and resources for children living in remote villages.He said that Himachal Pradesh has made remarkable progress in the field of quality education. In 2021, the state ranked 21st in the country, whereas it has now improved to the fifth position. The state govt has introduced English-medium education from Class I and implemented the CBSE curriculum in 156 govt schools. Preparations are also underway to open 100 additional CBSE schools from the next academic session. The chief minister said that the availability of qualified teachers is essential for ensuring quality education. In this direction, 10,000 posts have been filled in the Education Department, while recruitment of another 3,000 teachers is underway.He emphasised that the education of no meritorious student should be disrupted due to financial constraints. To promote equality in education, the state govt has decided to remove the caste-related column from school admission forms from the upcoming academic session. He said that children should be identified by their talent and hard work, while eligible families will continue to receive benefits under govt welfare schemes as before.The chief minister said that under the Dr. Y.S. Parmar Vidyarthi Rin Yojana, a loan of up to Rs 20 lakh is being provided at an interest rate of one per cent for pursuing higher education in India and abroad. Under the Indira Gandhi Sukh Shiksha Yojana, govt bears the entire cost of education in govt institutions for eligible children of widows and parents with disabilities who secure admission to professional and higher education courses. He further stated that during the last two years, scholarships amounting to approximately Rs. 92 crore have been provided to more than 88,000 students. The state govt, he asserted, will not compromise on the quality of education under any circumstances.The chief minister said that along with education, healthcare and the rural economy are also among the govt's key priorities.
